cell_types.name: Neural progenitor cells
cell_types.summary: Proliferating PAX6+/SOX2+ neuroepithelial cells, the common ancestor of every CNS neuron and glial cell. Almost all CNS differentiation protocols pass through this stage, so it is the point at which regional identity is set and the stage most often banked, expanded or patterned.
cell_types.maturation_note: PAX6 by day 7-11 and >80-95% purity by day 11-15; rosettes with apical ZO-1 appear after the first passage. Patterning has to be applied in a narrow window (around day 5 to day 18 depending on protocol) - after that, regional identity is largely fixed.

morphology.endpoint: A dense sheet of small, tightly packed columnar cells with almost no cytoplasm visible between nuclei, organised into radial rosettes with a bright central lumen. Mitotic figures sit at the lumen. Flatter, more spread cells at the colony edges are usually non-neural contamination.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat, compact colonies of small cells with sharp borders and a high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio.

stages.label: Even monolayer
stages.look: The culture has filled in to a uniform near-confluent sheet; gaps or uneven density here predict patchy induction.

stages.label: Neuroectoderm
stages.look: Cells become smaller and more uniform, and the sheet starts to look multilayered and refractile under phase.

stages.label: Neuroepithelium
stages.look: A thick, pseudostratified sheet of columnar cells; the surface looks optically bright and slightly ridged.

stages.label: Neural rosettes
stages.look: Clear radial rosettes 100-300 um across with a bright central lumen; three to ten per colony is typical.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be gone by about day 5 of dual SMAD inhibition; persistence means incomplete induction.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Lost rapidly after SB431542 is added - the Activin/Nodal block is what collapses it.

markers.name: FGF5
markers.note: Peaks around day 5 with OTX2, marking the transient epiblast-like state between pluripotency and neural fate.

markers.name: SOX1
markers.note: The earliest neural marker in dual SMAD inhibition, appearing before ZIC1 and PAX6.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: The standard purity readout: >80% at day 11 (Chambers) and >95% at day 15 with a retinoid (Shi).

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Pan-neural-stem-cell; also expressed in pluripotent cells, so never use it alone.

markers.name: NES
markers.note: General neural stem/progenitor marker; broad but useful for morphology.

markers.name: TJP1
markers.note: Apical ZO-1 ringing the rosette lumen is the sign of a properly polarised neuroepithelium.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Anterior/telencephalic identity; raised by WNT inhibition with XAV939 or DKK1.

markers.name: OTX2
markers.note: Anterior marker retained through neural commitment; also an epiblast marker at day 5.

markers.name: NGFR
markers.note: Marks the neural crest fraction. Low plating density pushes the culture this way; with PAX6-negative cells also expressing AP2, HNK1 and PAX7.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: Neural crest; should be absent in a CNS progenitor prep.

markers.name: HOXB4
markers.note: Caudal identity. Absent in anterior/cortical cultures; expected (deliberately) in spinal protocols.

markers.name: T
markers.note: Mesoderm escape; suppressed by SB431542.

functional_assays: Rosette formation after passage
Interkinetic nuclear migration by time-lapse
Apical mitoses (phospho-histone H3 at the lumen)
Response to patterning factors (SHH, RA, WNT)
qc: PAX6+ >= 80% by flow or ICC at day 11 (Chambers 2009)
OCT4 negative by day 5-7
T (brachyury) and SOX17 not detectable by qPCR
p75/HNK1 neural crest fraction low
Apical ZO-1 in rosettes after the first passage

protocols.name: Dual-SMAD inhibition (Noggin + SB431542)
protocols.principle: Blocking BMP and Activin/Nodal/TGF-beta signalling at the same time strips away the signals that keep hPSCs pluripotent or push them to mesendoderm and trophoblast, so an adherent monolayer converts almost entirely to PAX6+ neuroepithelium in under two weeks.

source.authors: Chambers SM, Fasano CA, Papapetrou EP, Tomishima M, Sadelain M, Studer L
source.title: Highly efficient neural conversion of human ES and iPS cells by dual inhibition of SMAD signaling.

protocols.efficiency: >80% PAX6+ cells at day 11; 82% reporter-positive neural precursors at day 13 by flow, about 3-fold more than the MS5 stromal-feeder protocol
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC dissociated to single cells with Accutase, pre-plated on gelatin to remove feeders, then plated on Matrigel at 10,000-25,000 cells/cm2 (18,000 cells/cm2 optimal) in MEF-conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/mL FGF2 and ROCK inhibitor; expand ~3 days to near confluence before day 0. Plating density sets the CNS vs neural crest ratio.

stages.name: Pre-plating and expansion
stages.base_medium: MEF-conditioned hESC medium (DMEM/F12, 20% knockout serum replacement, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol)

factors.name: FGF2
factors.role: keeps cells undifferentiated while they attach and spread

factors.name: Y-27632 (ROCK inhibitor)
factors.role: single-cell survival; withdrawn after the first day

actions: Dissociate with Accutase for ~20 min and pre-plate on gelatin for 1 h to deplete feeders
Plate the non-adherent PSCs on Matrigel at ~18,000 cells/cm2
Withdraw ROCK inhibitor after 24 h and let the culture reach near confluence
stages.checkpoint: Even, near-confluent monolayer with no gaps - uneven density gives patchy induction

stages.name: Dual SMAD inhibition

factors.name: Noggin
factors.role: BMP antagonist; suppresses CDX2/trophoblast and endoderm

factors.name: SB431542
factors.conc: 10 uM (the paper's methods text prints 10 nM)
factors.role: ALK4/5/7 inhibitor; collapses NANOG and blocks mesoderm

actions: Switch to KSR medium with both inhibitors on day 0
Expect OCT4 to be lost by about day 5
stages.checkpoint: Peak FGF5 and OTX2 around day 5 marks the transient epiblast-like state; OCT4 should be gone

stages.name: SMAD block narrowed, N2 ramp
stages.base_medium: KSR medium progressively replaced by N2 medium (25%, 50%, 75% every two days)
stages.feeding: Medium change every two days with increasing N2 fraction
actions: Withdraw SB431542 on day 5
Step the N2 fraction up every two days while keeping Noggin
Score PAX6 by day 11; passage at day 11-12 if you intend to pattern or make rosettes
stages.checkpoint: >80% PAX6+ nuclei; SOX1 rises first, then ZIC1/PAX6, then FOXG1

tips: The authors note comparable neural conversion when the inhibitors are given only for the first 5 days, which saves a lot of recombinant Noggin.
Most labs now swap Noggin for the small-molecule ALK2/3 inhibitor LDN-193189 (100 nM); that LSB variant is the backbone of the Maroof, Tchieu and Kim/Studer protocols.
Early neuroepithelium here is non-polarised; rosettes with apical ZO-1 appear after the first passage.
pitfalls: Low plating density shifts the output to PAX6-negative neural crest (AP2, HNK1, PAX7, p75) instead of CNS.
Very high density blunts the response to patterning factors, so pattern around day 5 and passage near day 11.
SB431542 alone drives CDX2/trophoblast; Noggin alone leaves <10% PAX6+ - both inhibitors are needed.
unverified: SB431542 dose: the published methods state 10 nM, which is widely treated as a typographical error; 10 uM is the dose used in the authors' later LSB protocols. Confirm against your own reference before use.
Y-27632 concentration not stated in the paper's methods.

protocols.name: LSB (+XAV939) to dorsal forebrain NSCs and rosettes
protocols.principle: A fully small-molecule update of dual-SMAD inhibition in Essential 6 medium: LDN-193189 replaces Noggin, and a short pulse of the tankyrase inhibitor XAV939 holds the cells anterior, giving dorsal forebrain neural stem cells that can be re-plated as droplets to form rosettes.

source.authors: Tchieu J, Calder EL, Guttikonda SR, et al.
source.title: NFIA is a gliogenic switch enabling rapid derivation of functional human astrocytes from pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated to single cells and plated on Matrigel at 2.5-3.0 x 10^5 cells/cm2 in Essential 8 with 10 uM Y-27632 the day before day 0.

stages.name: Dual SMAD inhibition (anteriorised)

factors.name: XAV939
factors.role: tankyrase/WNT inhibitor, days 0-2 only; reinforces forebrain (FOXG1) identity - recommended for iPSC lines

actions: Start LSB on day 0 and change medium every day through day 8
Add XAV939 for the first three days only, then continue with LSB alone
stages.checkpoint: Uniform neuroepithelial sheet by day 8

stages.name: Rosette formation
stages.base_medium: N2 medium with BDNF, ascorbic acid, SHH and FGF8 (N2-BASF)

factors.name: SHH
factors.role: component of the N2-BASF rosette medium

factors.name: FGF8
factors.role: component of the N2-BASF rosette medium

actions: Dissociate with Accutase for 30 min, pass through a 40 um strainer
Re-plate as high-density droplets on air-dried poly-ornithine/laminin/fibronectin, let them attach 15-20 min, then overlay with medium
Expect rosettes 2-3 days later (around day 11-12)
stages.checkpoint: Radially organised rosettes; re-plate at high density (3.5 x 10^5 cells/cm2) to stop spontaneous differentiation

tips: The same paper gives the ventral spinal cord variant: LSB from day 0 with 1 uM retinoic acid plus 1 uM purmorphamine added from day 1 to day 12 - a convenient way to get regionally matched progenitors.
These NSCs are neurogenic for months; glial competence has to be forced (see the NFIA astrocyte protocol).
pitfalls: Passaging rosette-stage NSCs at low density lets them differentiate spontaneously.
Dropping XAV939 can let iPSC lines drift posterior and lose FOXG1.
unverified: Concentrations of SHH, FGF8, BDNF and ascorbic acid in N2-BASF are not given in the paper text.
Exact droplet cell number is garbled in the available full text.

cell_types.notes: Plating density is the hidden variable: Chambers and colleagues showed it sets the ratio of CNS to neural crest progeny, with high density favouring PAX6+ CNS cells. Noggin is now usually replaced by LDN-193189 (100 nM), giving the 'LSB' backbone used by most downstream protocols in this slice. Decide your regional identity before you start - the patterning window is early, and an unpatterned culture defaults to dorsal forebrain.

cell_types.name: Cortical excitatory neurons
cell_types.summary: Glutamatergic projection neurons of the cerebral cortex, about 80% of cortical neurons, generated in a fixed deep-to-superficial temporal order. They are the workhorse of hPSC disease modelling for Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, autism and epilepsy, and the substrate for most human synaptic-function assays.
cell_types.maturation_note: Directed differentiation: TBR1+ layer-6 neurons within days of neurogenesis onset, BRN2/CUX1 from days 25-30, SATB2 from days 65-80, astrocytes from about day 60. AMPA-mediated synapses by day 50 and action-potential trains by day 65. Transcription-factor programming compresses this to about 14 days but gives an immature layer 2/3-like neuron with no NMDA receptors at 3 weeks.

morphology.endpoint: A dense network of small, round-to-pyramidal cell bodies connected by long, branched neurites that cross and bundle into fascicles. In directed-differentiation cultures the neurons sit in clumps around residual rosettes with flat astrocytes appearing underneath after about two months.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact flat colonies with sharp edges; neural induction only starts once they are about 95% confluent.

stages.label: Cortical neuroepithelium
stages.look: A thick, bright pseudostratified sheet of columnar cells with no visible gaps.

stages.label: Cortical rosettes
stages.look: Radial rosettes with apical lumens; mitoses at the lumen and a rim of smaller Tbr2+ cells at the periphery.

stages.label: Early neurogenesis
stages.look: Short neurites emerge from the rosette edges; a mesh of fine processes starts to cover the space between rosettes.

stages.label: Layered cortical network
stages.look: Dense neurite network with bundled fascicles, neuronal cell bodies piled above the progenitor layer.

stages.label: Mixed neurons and astrocytes
stages.look: Flat stellate astrocytes spread under the neuronal network from about day 60 onwards.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent; in NGN2 programming, SOX2, OCT4 and NANOG immunoreactivity is gone by day 21.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: >95% at day 15 in the retinoid-dependent Shi/Livesey protocol; only ~25% without retinoids.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Telencephalic identity. Also induced strongly in NGN2 iN cells.

markers.name: EMX1
markers.note: Dorsal telencephalic; high in cortical rosettes and absent in ventralised cultures.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Basal/intermediate progenitors at the rosette rim; about 15% of rosette cells at day 25, roughly half of them still cycling.

markers.name: TBR1
markers.note: First projection-neuron subtype to appear; peaks at about 41% of cells at day 76 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: BCL11B
markers.note: Subcortical projection neurons; high early then declining. Only ~3% of cells co-express CTIP2 and SATB2, as expected for mutually exclusive programmes.

markers.name: SATB2
markers.note: Late marker, from days 65-80 in 2D and rising up to 7-fold between days 52 and 137 in spheroids - the honest test of whether a culture has been run long enough.

markers.name: POU3F2
markers.note: Layer 2-4 and late progenitors; peaks before SATB2. Also high in NGN2 iN cells.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: Pan-neuronal dendritic marker; used to score conversion efficiency in programming protocols.

markers.name: RBFOX3
markers.note: Only appears in human forebrain after about 20 weeks gestation; 36 +/- 4% of cells at day 76 in spheroids.

markers.name: SLC17A7
markers.note: Presynaptic glutamate transporter; co-localises with PSD95 at excitatory synapses. NGN2 neurons express mostly SLC17A6 (VGLUT2) with VGLUT1 in about 20% of cells.

markers.name: DLG4
markers.note: About 90% of PSD95 puncta sit within one puncta-diameter of synaptophysin, i.e. they are real synapses.

markers.name: GAD1
markers.note: Should be absent: cortical interneurons come from the ventral telencephalon and are not made by these protocols. Its appearance means the culture has been ventralised.

functional_assays: Whole-cell patch clamp: action potential trains, TTX-sensitive sodium currents
Spontaneous and evoked EPSCs blocked by CNQX/NBQX
Calcium imaging (Fura-2 or GCaMP) of network activity
Acute slice recording from cortical spheroids
BrdU/EdU birthdating to confirm the deep-to-superficial order
Super-resolution or array tomography of pre/post-synaptic puncta
qc: PAX6+ > 90-95% at day 15 before the onset of neurogenesis
Roughly equal deep (TBR1/CTIP2) and upper (SATB2/BRN2) layer neurons by day 70 in directed differentiation
CNQX-sensitive mEPSCs recordable by day 50
No GAD67+ cells in a dorsal cortical prep
For NGN2 programming: >90% of transduced cells MAP2+ or NeuN+

protocols.name: Retinoid + dual SMAD inhibition: cortical rosettes to layered projection neurons
protocols.principle: Dual SMAD inhibition in a 1:1 N2/B27 medium plus retinoid signalling turns hPSCs into dorsal forebrain rosettes containing apical and basal progenitors; withdrawing FGF2 then lets them run a months-long, developmentally ordered wave of neurogenesis from deep- to upper-layer neurons.

source.authors: Shi Y, Kirwan P, Smith J, Robinson HPC, Livesey FJ
source.title: Human cerebral cortex development from pluripotent stem cells to functional excitatory synapses.

protocols.efficiency: >95% PAX6+/OTX1/2+/vimentin+ cortical progenitors 15 days after induction; roughly equal numbers of deep- and upper-layer projection neurons by day 70; without retinoids only ~25% PAX6+
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC dissociated with Accutase, pre-plated 1 h on gelatin to deplete feeders, then plated on Matrigel-coated 12-well plates in MEF-conditioned hESC medium with 10 ng/mL FGF2. Neural induction only begins once the monolayer is 95% confluent.

stages.name: Neural induction
stages.base_medium: 3N medium: 1:1 N2 medium (DMEM/F12, N2, 5 ug/mL insulin, glutamine, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol) and B27 medium (Neurobasal + B27)

factors.name: Dorsomorphin
factors.role: BMP inhibitor (or 500 ng/mL mouse Noggin-CF chimera instead)

factors.name: Retinoids (retinol acetate and all-trans retinol)
factors.role: required for efficient cortical induction in human cells; B27 with vitamin A is the usual source

stages.feeding: Medium change every other day; maintain 8-11 days
actions: Switch the confluent monolayer to 3N medium with both SMAD inhibitors on day 0
Watch for columnar neuroepithelial morphology appearing over days 8-11
stages.checkpoint: Near-uniform neuroepithelial morphology; >95% PAX6+/OTX1/2+ by day 15 of the overall process

stages.name: Rosette expansion

factors.name: FGF2
factors.role: expands rosette progenitors and holds back neurogenesis

actions: Lift neuroepithelium with Dispase and re-plate onto poly-ornithine/laminin
Keep FGF2 for 2 days after re-plating, then withdraw it to start neurogenesis
stages.checkpoint: Rosettes with apical ZO-1/N-cadherin, apical mitoses and interkinetic nuclear migration; Tbr2+ basal progenitors at the rosette rim (~15% of cells at day 25)

stages.name: Cortical neurogenesis
actions: Passage once more with Accutase and re-plate at 50,000 cells/cm2 on poly-ornithine/laminin
Keep feeding every other day; neurons can be held for up to 100 days
stages.checkpoint: TBR1+ layer-6 neurons first, then CTIP2, then BRN2/CUX1 from days 25-30, SATB2 from days 65-80

stages.name: Maturation, synapses and late astrogenesis
actions: Record or image from day 50 onward
Expect S100+ astrocytes from about day 60, increasing over the next 40 days
stages.checkpoint: Repetitive action-potential trains by about day 65; CNQX-sensitive mEPSCs and evoked EPSPs from day 50

materials: N2 and B27 (with vitamin A) supplements
tips: The step-by-step version of this method is Shi Y, Kirwan P, Livesey FJ, Nat Protoc 2012;7:1836-46 (PMID 22976355, doi 10.1038/nprot.2012.116), described there as an 80-day three-stage process.
No GABAergic interneurons arise under these conditions - the cortex gets its interneurons from the ventral telencephalon, so add them separately if you want balanced networks.
Early rosettes stay plastic: purmorphamine ventralises them and yields GAD67+ interneurons instead.
pitfalls: Dropping the retinoid leaves only scattered PAX6+ patches (~25%) - this is the step most often got wrong.
Inhibiting hedgehog signalling does not help cortical induction in human cells, contrary to the mouse rule of thumb.
Upper-layer (SATB2+) neurons simply need time; cultures ended at day 40 will look deep-layer biased.
unverified: Retinoid identities are given (retinol acetate, all-trans retinol) but concentrations are not stated in the paper's methods.
Day boundaries for induction are a range (8-11 days) in the source; 10 is used here as the typical value.

protocols.name: NGN2 forced expression (one transcription factor, ~2 weeks)
protocols.principle: Doxycycline-inducible neurogenin-2 converts hPSCs directly into excitatory, layer 2/3-like forebrain neurons in under two weeks, bypassing progenitor stages; mouse glia are added to support synapse formation.

source.authors: Zhang Y, Pak C, Han Y, et al.
source.title: Rapid single-step induction of functional neurons from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: Nearly 100% of surviving transduced cells become neurons; single-cell profiling shows a homogeneous excitatory population whose properties are indistinguishable across one ESC and two iPSC lines

factors.conc: 0.3 uL per well of a 24-well plate

factors.name: Polybrene
factors.conc: 8 ug/uL as stated in the paper

actions: Plate dissociated hPSCs on Matrigel on day -2
Add lentivirus in fresh mTeSR1 on day -1
stages.checkpoint: Use only virus preparations giving >90% infection

stages.name: NGN2 induction and selection

factors.conc: 2 g/L as stated in the paper (i.e. 2 ug/mL)
factors.role: switches on TetO-NGN2; kept in the medium to the end

stages.feeding: Switch medium on day 0; puromycin for 24 h from day 1

Run a 24 h puromycin selection starting day 1
stages.checkpoint: SOX2/nestin spike then fall sharply; neuron-like morphology within a week

stages.name: Glia co-culture and maturation

factors.name: Ara-C
factors.conc: 2 g/L as stated in the paper

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.conc: 2 g/L as stated in the paper

stages.feeding: Exchange 50% of the medium every 2 days

Add Ara-C with the glia; add 2.5% FBS from day 10

stages.checkpoint: Mature morphology by two weeks; spontaneous AMPA-mediated EPSCs blocked by CNQX; NMDA currents only appear after about 4 weeks

tips: NeuroD1 works about as well as NGN2 in this system; the authors chose NGN2 and stayed with it.
The neurons are telencephalic and excitatory (BRN2, CUX1, FOXG1, vGLUT2 with some vGLUT1) and read as relatively immature layer 2/3; they lack vGAT and GAD.
Co-culture with mouse cortical neurons rather than glia alone adds inhibitory inputs and lets the human neurons integrate into a network.
pitfalls: Astrocyte support is doing real work here: without mouse glia, synapse formation is poor.
The population is deliberately homogeneous, which is a liability if your phenotype lives in a specific neuronal subtype.
NMDA receptors are essentially absent at 3 weeks - plan longer culture if you need them.
unverified: Several concentrations are quoted in the paper in unusual units (doxycycline 2 g/L, Ara-C 2 g/L, polybrene 8 ug/uL); they are reproduced as printed rather than converted.

protocols.name: i3Neurons: NGN2 at a safe-harbour locus, 3-day induction
protocols.principle: Instead of fresh lentivirus each time, NGN2 is stably integrated at a safe-harbour locus under a doxycycline-inducible promoter and the clone is isolated, so a simple two-step protocol gives near-pure cortical neurons and lets partially differentiated cells be banked frozen.

source.authors: Fernandopulle MS, Prestil R, Grunseich C, Wang C, Gan L, Ward ME
source.title: Transcription Factor-Mediated Differentiation of Human iPSCs into Neurons.

protocols.efficiency: Reported as near 100% efficiency and purity of glutamatergic cortical neurons within the 14-day timeline for the integrated clonal line
protocols.start_requirements: A clonal iPSC line with a stably integrated doxycycline-inducible NGN2 transgene, 70-80% confluent and free of spontaneous differentiation, in E8 (or equivalent) on Matrigel.

stages.name: Induction on Matrigel
stages.feeding: Full medium change with freshly supplemented IM daily on days 1 and 2

Wash once with PBS and refresh IM + doxycycline on days 1 and 2
Check for obvious neurites by day 3

stages.name: Replating and maturation

factors.name: Laminin
factors.role: included in CM to support outgrowth

stages.feeding: Half-medium change with fresh CM every 7 days beyond day 10
actions: Dissociate with Accutase on day 3 and either freeze stocks or replate onto freshly coated poly-L-ornithine dishes

cell_types.notes: Choose the route by what you need. Directed differentiation gives the real developmental sequence, progenitor diversity (including outer radial glia) and all layer identities, but takes 70-100 days and varies between lines. Transcription-factor programming gives a homogeneous, reproducible population in two weeks - the Zhang paper's central point was that NGN2 overrides epigenetic differences between lines - but the neurons are immature layer 2/3-like cells, lack NMDA receptors at 3 weeks, and need glia (usually mouse astrocytes) to form synapses. The i3Neuron version removes the virus from the workflow altogether. No protocol here makes interneurons: they must be added separately.

cell_types.name: Midbrain dopaminergic neurons
cell_types.summary: Substantia nigra and ventral tegmental dopamine neurons, defined by co-expression of the floor-plate factor FOXA2 with the midbrain factor LMX1A on top of tyrosine hydroxylase. They are the cell lost in Parkinson's disease and the most clinically advanced hPSC-derived neuron, with the Studer and Lund protocols now feeding first-in-human trials.
cell_types.maturation_note: Engraftable precursors by day 16-25. In vitro the neurons are still immature at day 40 (resting potential about -35 mV, single action potential only); by day 60-75 they have adult-like properties, HCN and KCNQ currents, 1-3 Hz pacemaking and calcium-dependent dopamine release. Behavioural recovery after grafting takes 3-5 months.

morphology.endpoint: A dense carpet of small neuronal cell bodies with very long, thin, often bundled neurites; after 50+ days the processes form thick fascicles and the culture looks fibrous. Re-plating at high density is part of the protocol, so the monolayer is thick and uneven.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Dense single-cell monolayer plated at 4 x 10^5 cells/cm2 - much denser than most neural inductions.

stages.label: Ventralised neuroepithelium
stages.look: Uniform, tightly packed sheet; no rosettes should form, which distinguishes the floor-plate route from the rosette route.

stages.label: Midbrain floor plate
stages.look: A flat, compact sheet of small cells; the key readout here is immunostaining (FOXA2/LMX1A/EN1), not morphology.

stages.label: mDA precursors
stages.look: Cells start to round up and extend short processes; this is the cryopreservation and grafting stage.

stages.label: Young mDA neurons
stages.look: Clear neuronal morphology with branched neurites over a background of flatter cells.

stages.label: Mature mDA network
stages.look: Long fasciculated neurites and larger, angular, often multipolar cell bodies (the GIRK2+/A9-like ones).

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent before grafting; residual pluripotent cells are the main teratoma risk.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Floor-plate identity. Requires strong SHH activation (purmorphamine with or without recombinant SHH).

markers.name: LMX1A
markers.note: Induced in FOXA2+ cells by CHIR99021; FOXA2/LMX1A co-expression is the midbrain signature and the day-11 go/no-go check.

markers.name: OTX2
markers.note: Must be retained: sustained high CHIR loses OTX2 and the culture turns hindbrain.

markers.name: EN1
markers.note: The marker the CHIR-boost protocol was built around; robust EN1 at day 11 predicts clean midbrain identity, and EN1 knockout lines lose the benefit of the boost.

markers.name: NR4A2
markers.note: Marks cell-cycle exit; the Kriks grafting stage (about day 25) was chosen around its onset.

markers.name: TH
markers.note: Necessary but not sufficient - rosette-derived cultures also make TH+ cells, which lack FOXA2/LMX1A and overgrow after grafting.

markers.name: PITX3

protocols.name: Midbrain floor-plate route (LSB/S/F8/CHIR)
protocols.principle: Strong SHH activation makes FOXA2+ floor plate, and adding the GSK3-beta inhibitor CHIR99021 induces LMX1A in those floor-plate cells - the FOXA2/LMX1A co-expression that is unique to the midbrain. Floor-plate-derived dopamine neurons engraft, whereas rosette-derived ones overgrow.

source.authors: Kriks S, Shim JW, Piao J, et al.
source.title: Dopamine neurons derived from human ES cells efficiently engraft in animal models of Parkinson's disease.

factors.name: Purmorphamine

Add CHIR99021 from day 3 and keep it to day 11

source.title: Biphasic Activation of WNT Signaling Facilitates the Derivation of Midbrain Dopamine Neurons from hESCs for Translational Use.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs on vitronectin in Essential 8, passaged with EDTA, used between passage 35-55; dissociated with Accutase and plated at 4 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on Geltrex for day 0.

stages.name: Low-CHIR floor-plate induction

actions: Plate at 4 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on Geltrex in the full cocktail (day 0)

Withdraw LDN, SB and SHH on day 7
stages.checkpoint: Day 11: EN1 high, FOXA2/LMX1A/OTX2 maintained, PAX6 (forebrain) and hindbrain/diencephalic markers low

factors.role: tapered WNT at the switch to differentiation medium

stages.feeding: Per schedule, with replating on day 11

Dissociate on day 11 and replate at 8 x 10^5 cells/cm2 on poly-ornithine (15 ug/mL) / laminin (1 ug/mL) / fibronectin (2 ug/mL)

stages.feeding: Replate on day 16 and again on day 25

materials: BDNF, GDNF, TGF-beta3, ascorbic acid, dibutyryl-cAMP
tips: Timing of the boost matters: boosting at day 3 strongly induced an unwanted non-mDA progenitor marker, and boosting above 7.5 uM caused dose-dependent cell death - day 4 at 7.5 uM was the optimum.

CHIR potency is medium-dependent: KSR-based media contain lysophosphatidic acid that blunts CHIR, which is why 'standard' doses range from 0.4-1 uM in defined medium but ~3 uM in KSR. Titrate for your medium and lot.
Late FGF8b gives EN1 levels as good as the boost but raises COL1A1 (perivascular fibroblast-like) and other contaminants - the reason this protocol avoids exogenous FGF8.
EN1 knockout lines lose the benefit of the boost, which is the authors' evidence that EN1 is the mediator.
pitfalls: Batch-to-batch variability in EN1 induction at a fixed CHIR dose is the classic failure mode; small dose differences flip the culture to hindbrain or diencephalic fate.
Holding high CHIR throughout ('High Chir') loses OTX2 and induces hindbrain markers.
Initial graft survival is usually under 10% of the cells injected, so dose accordingly.
A9 versus A10 proportions are still not controllable.

cell_types.notes: This is the cell type where protocols genuinely disagree, and the disagreement is about CHIR99021. Published doses span 0.4-1 uM in defined medium and about 3 uM in KSR-based medium, because knockout serum replacement contains lysophosphatidic acid that blunts CHIR; the CHIR-boost protocol adds a second, 7.5 uM phase from day 4. Kim and colleagues documented dramatic batch-to-batch swings in EN1 induction at an identical 0.7 uM dose, so the dose must be titrated per medium, per lot and per line, with EN1 at day 11 as the readout. The FGF8 question is similarly unsettled: Kirkeby/Nolbrant use late FGF8b to refine midbrain identity (Nolbrant S, Heuer A, Parmar M, Kirkeby A, Nat Protoc 2017;12:1962-79; PMID 28858290, doi 10.1038/nprot.2017.078), while Kim and colleagues avoid it because it raises COL1A1+ and hindbrain contaminants. Kirkeby A, Grealish S, Wolf DA, et al., Cell Rep 2012;1:703-14 (PMID 22813745, doi 10.1016/j.celrep.2012.04.009) is the original dose-dependent WNT patterning paper.

cell_types.name: Spinal motor neurons
cell_types.summary: Cholinergic neurons of the ventral spinal cord that project to skeletal muscle, derived through the OLIG2+ pMN progenitor domain by caudalising with WNT/retinoic acid and ventralising with a SHH agonist. They are the central cell type for ALS and spinal muscular atrophy modelling and for neuromuscular junction assays.
cell_types.maturation_note: OLIG2+ progenitors by day 12, MNX1/ISL1+ neurons by day 18, and CHAT+ functionally mature motor neurons after a further 10 days of Notch inhibition. Notch inhibition is what makes the difference: without it only about 47% of cells are CHAT+ after two weeks, with it 91%.

morphology.endpoint: Large neuronal cell bodies, noticeably bigger than cortical neurons, with thick primary processes and long axons that often run in bundles. In Notch-inhibited cultures the background is clean, with no small dividing cells between the neurons.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Colonies split 1:6 the day before induction; no spontaneous differentiation.

stages.label: Caudal neuroepithelium
stages.look: A uniform dense sheet of small cells, more than 98% SOX1+, that looks the same as any neuroepithelium under phase - the HOX identity is only visible by staining.

stages.label: OLIG2+ pMN progenitors
stages.look: Still a dense progenitor monolayer; expandable, and spheres re-form readily when the cells are lifted.

stages.label: Motor neuron precursors
stages.look: Round suspension aggregates from which neurons emerge once plated; MNX1/ISL1 positive.

stages.label: Mature motor neurons
stages.look: Large cell bodies with thick processes on Matrigel or an astrocyte feeder; no proliferating cells remain after Compound E.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent.

markers.name: SOX1
markers.note: >98% at day 6 with CHIR + SB431542 + DMH-1; CHIR also raises the absolute yield about 2.8-fold.

markers.name: HOXA3
markers.note: Confirms caudalisation; without CHIR the cells stay rostral and express OTX2 instead.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: 95 +/- 3% at day 12 with CHIR/SB/DMH-1/RA/purmorphamine; the expandable progenitor stage.

markers.name: NKX2-2
markers.note: The marker most often missed: with RA + SHH alone up to 40% of OLIG2+ cells also express NKX2-2, which blocks their differentiation into motor neurons. WNT keeps it off; good cultures have <0.5% double positives.

markers.name: MNX1
markers.note: 90 +/- 9% at day 18 in the Du protocol.

markers.name: ISL1
markers.note: 95 +/- 3% at day 18; also one of the programming factors in the hNIL cassette.

markers.name: CHAT
markers.note: 91 +/- 6% of MAP2+ cells after 10 days of Compound E, versus 47 +/- 9% without it.

markers.name: FOXP1
markers.note: FOXP1+/LHX3-negative marks limb-innervating lateral motor column identity, the subtype enriched by the Amoroso protocol.

markers.name: LHX3
markers.note: Columnar subtype marker; also one of the hNIL programming factors.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: Pan-neuronal; the denominator for CHAT+ percentages.

markers.name: NEFL
markers.note: Reduced about 45% in SOD1 D90A motor neurons but not in GABA neurons from the same line - a motor-neuron-specific disease readout.

markers.name: MKI67
markers.note: Should be undetectable after Compound E; 40-50% of cells are Ki-67+ during expansion.

markers.name: GAD1
markers.note: What you get if SHH signalling is blocked (cyclopamine instead of purmorphamine) - a useful isogenic control but a contaminant otherwise.

protocols.name: Small-molecule OLIG2+ motor neuron progenitors, expandable
protocols.principle: CHIR99021 with dual SMAD inhibition makes caudal neuroepithelium in one step; adding retinoic acid and purmorphamine ventralises it to a near-pure OLIG2+ (pMN) progenitor, with WNT suppressing the neighbouring NKX2-2+ p3 fate. The progenitors can be expanded, and a Notch inhibitor then synchronises their conversion into mature motor neurons.

source.authors: Du ZW, Chen H, Liu H, et al.
source.title: Generation and expansion of highly pure motor neuron progenitors from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: >98% SOX1+ neuroepithelium at day 6; 95 +/- 3% OLIG2+ progenitors at day 12 with <0.5% OLIG2/NKX2-2 double positives; 90 +/- 9% MNX1+ and 95 +/- 3% ISL1+ at day 18; 91 +/- 6% of MAP2+ neurons CHAT+ after 10 days of Compound E; reproducible in IMR90, ALS (SOD1 D90A, A4V) and SMA lines
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated with Dispase (1 mg/mL) and split 1:6 onto irradiated MEFs or Matrigel; the next day switch to the chemically defined neural medium (1:1 DMEM/F12 : Neurobasal, 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27, 0.1 mM ascorbic acid, Glutamax, pen/strep).

stages.base_medium: 1:1 DMEM/F12 : Neurobasal with 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27, 0.1 mM ascorbic acid, Glutamax

factors.name: CHIR99021

factors.role: Notch/gamma-secretase inhibitor; removes dividing precursors and speeds maturation

factors.role: added only if plating at low density

actions: Dissociate the day-18 MNs to single cells with Accumax and plate on Matrigel or astrocytes

Swapping purmorphamine for cyclopamine in the same schedule yields OLIG2-negative spinal GABA neurons, a convenient isogenic non-motor-neuron control.

protocols.name: i3LMNs: NGN2 + ISL1 + LHX3 (hNIL) at a safe-harbour locus
protocols.principle: Adding ISL1 and LHX3 to inducible NGN2 at a safe-harbour locus programmes iPSCs directly into lower motor neurons on the same three-day induction schedule as i3Neurons, with a Notch inhibitor from day 1.

protocols.start_requirements: A clonal iPSC line with doxycycline-inducible hNIL (NGN2, ISL1, LHX3) transgenes, healthy and not over-confluent; seed one 10 cm dish with 1.5 x 10^6 cells (2 x 10^4 iPSC/cm2).

cell_types.notes: Two things set the good protocols apart from the old 1-2 month, 30-70% efficient ones. First, WNT activation: CHAR99021 both caudalises in a single step and, crucially, separates the OLIG2 (pMN) and NKX2-2 (p3) domains - staining for NKX2-2 as well as OLIG2 is the most useful diagnostic if a culture is OLIG2-high but motor-neuron-poor. Second, Notch inhibition (Compound E or DAPT) at the differentiation step, which synchronises the progenitors and removes residual dividing cells. Related protocols worth comparing: Maury Y, Come J, Piskorowski RA, et al., Nat Biotechnol 2015;33:89-96 (PMID 25383599, doi 10.1038/nbt.3049), a combinatorial small-molecule screen that produced 14-day spinal and cranial motor neuron protocols and first highlighted the role of canonical WNT; and Amoroso MW, Croft GF, Williams DJ, et al., J Neurosci 2013;33:574-86 (PMID 23303937, doi 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0906-12.2013), which reaches up to 50% motor neurons in 3 weeks and preferentially gives limb-innervating FOXP1+/LHX3-negative lateral motor column neurons. Neither of those two could be verified at the level of stage concentrations in this session, so they are cited rather than written out.

cell_types.name: Cortical GABAergic interneurons
cell_types.summary: Inhibitory, locally projecting neurons that make up about 20% of cortical neurons and are born in the ventral telencephalon before migrating tangentially into the cortex. Their dysfunction is implicated in schizophrenia, autism and epilepsy, and they are needed to build balanced excitatory-inhibitory networks from hPSCs.
cell_types.maturation_note: MGE-like progenitors at day 18 and migratory precursors by day 32, but functional maturation is genuinely slow: on a mouse cortical feeder the neurons reach fairly mature properties in about 30 days of co-culture, while the companion study reports an intrinsic timeline of up to 7 months for full subtype maturation, mirroring human development. Programming with ASCL1+DLX2 reaches synaptic maturity in about 5 weeks and keeps improving to 7 weeks.

morphology.endpoint: Small, often bipolar or multipolar neurons with fine, highly branched neurites, usually sitting on top of a feeder layer of cortical neurons and glia. Interneurons are visibly smaller and more delicate than the pyramidal neurons they sit on.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact flat colonies; XLSB starts on the attached monolayer.

stages.label: Forebrain neuroepithelium
stages.look: Uniform dense neuroepithelial sheet; FOXG1 and PAX6 positive, before any SHH exposure.

stages.label: MGE-like progenitors
stages.look: Still a progenitor monolayer, Nestin and Ki-67 positive; identity is defined by NKX2-1 and OLIG2 staining.

stages.label: Migratory precursors
stages.look: Ki-67 falls, DCX and TUJ1 rise; the cells are bipolar or unipolar with a leading process, the migratory morphology.

stages.label: Maturing interneurons
stages.look: Fine, densely branched neurites over the cortical feeder, with VGAT puncta along dendrites of neighbouring cells.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Must be absent.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Telencephalic identity; raised by XAV939. >90% of NKX2-1+ cells co-express it in the day 10-18 condition, whereas early SHH (days 2-18) suppresses it and gives hypothalamic cells.

markers.name: NKX2-1
markers.note: Ventral prosencephalic progenitors. Unlike mouse, human hPSC-derived interneurons keep expressing it after becoming postmitotic, so loss of NKX2-1 is not a maturity readout here.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: Nearly 80% of NKX2-1+ cells in the day 10-18 window; separates the ganglionic eminence from the OLIG2-negative preoptic anlage.

markers.name: LHX6
markers.note: Selectively enriched in the day 10-18 condition at day 32 - the best discriminator of MGE-like versus hypothalamic or cholinergic output.

markers.name: DLX2
markers.note: Pan-DLX staining is 88-92% positive in programmed GABAergic neurons; DLX2 is the second programming factor.

markers.name: GAD1
markers.note: With GAD2 (GAD65), 83-94% positive in programmed cultures.

markers.name: SLC32A1
markers.note: Presynaptic GABA transporter; its puncta should line up with postsynaptic gephyrin.

markers.name: GABA
markers.note: About 80% of sorted GFP+ cells after co-culture in the Maroof protocol; 81-89% in programmed cultures.

markers.name: SST
markers.note: About 37% of programmed AD-iN cells at 5 weeks; appears only in the day 10-18 condition in directed differentiation. Higher SHH favours SST over PV.

markers.name: PVALB
markers.note: The hardest subtype: about 5% of GFP+ cells by automated imaging, and only a subset look convincingly interneuron-like. PV is expressed late even in primate development.

markers.name: RAX
markers.note: Enriched when SHH is given early (days 2-18); the signature of the wrong ventral fate.

markers.name: TH
markers.note: Large numbers of TH+ cells in the early-SHH condition, consistent with NKX2-1-lineage hypothalamic neurons.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Counter-intuitive but real: FOXA2 is transiently expressed in the human telencephalic ganglionic eminence and in hPSC-derived NKX2-1+ cells, though not in mouse. Do not read it as floor-plate contamination.

protocols.name: XLSB + timed SHH: NKX2-1+ MGE-like progenitors to cortical interneurons
protocols.principle: WNT inhibition with XAV939 secures forebrain (FOXG1) identity, and then the timing of SHH activation decides which ventral progenitor you get: late SHH (days 10-18) gives FOXG1+/OLIG2+ MGE-like progenitors that migrate like cortical interneurons and mature into SST+ and PV+ cells.

source.authors: Maroof AM, Keros S, Tyson JA, et al.
source.title: Directed differentiation and functional maturation of cortical interneurons from human embryonic stem cells.
