stages.checkpoint: Strong FOXG1 induction; XAV939 can replace recombinant DKK1 here

stages.name: Timed SHH ventralisation
actions: Add SHH C25II and purmorphamine on day 10 and keep them to day 18
Do not start SHH earlier than day 6 if you want cortical interneurons
stages.checkpoint: Day 18: NKX2-1+ progenitors, >90% FOXG1+ and ~80% OLIG2+, also expressing ASCL1 and NKX6-2; note the transient human-specific FOXA2 expression, which is not a floor-plate artefact

stages.name: Neuronal differentiation
actions: Withdraw the SHH agonists after day 18
Expect Ki-67 to fall and DCX/TUJ1 to rise; GABA and calbindin appear
FACS-sort at about day 32 if using a reporter line
stages.checkpoint: Day 32: LHX6 protein enriched specifically in the day 10-18 condition (the MGE signature); RAX instead marks the early-SHH hypothalamic condition

stages.name: Co-culture maturation
stages.base_medium: Neurobasal + B27 on a mouse (E13.5) cortical feeder
stages.feeding: Per schedule for ~30 days of co-culture
actions: Replate sorted progenitors on dissociated E13.5 mouse cortex
Record after 20-30 days in vitro
stages.checkpoint: VGAT puncta matching gephyrin, bicuculline-sensitive spontaneous IPSCs, SST+ and PV+ neurons; no VIP or calretinin cells, i.e. no caudal ganglionic eminence output

tips: Timing of SHH, not its dose, is the lever: days 2-18 gives FOXG1-negative hypothalamic cells (RAX+, many TH+ and nNOS+), days 6-18 gives FOXG1+/OLIG2-negative cells enriched for cholinergic (ChAT+) neurons, days 10-18 gives the MGE-like interneuron progenitors.

Maturation is environment-dependent: on mouse cortical feeders the neurons mature noticeably faster than on hESC-derived human cortical feeders, which may simply reflect more astrocytes in the mouse prep.

Nicholas CR, Chen J, Tang Y, et al., Cell Stem Cell 2013;12:573-86 (PMID 23642366, doi 10.1016/j.stem.2013.04.005) is the companion study: MGE-like progenitors mature over an intrinsic timeline of up to 7 months, which is the realistic horizon for fully mature subtypes.
pitfalls: Human hPSC-derived interneurons keep expressing NKX2-1 after they become postmitotic, unlike mouse cells where Nkx2-1 is extinguished before they enter the cortex - so NKX2-1 loss is not a good maturity readout here, and some cells may be striatal rather than cortical interneurons.
PV+ cells are rare (~5%) and only a subset look convincingly interneuron-like; PV is a late marker.
Transplanted precursors stay immature for months, with immature growth cones at 3 months post-graft.
unverified: The paper lists SHH C25II over a 50-500 ng/mL range and purmorphamine at 1-2 uM; the stated maximal condition is 5 nM SHH with 1 uM purmorphamine. FGF2 at 5-10 ng/mL is listed among reagents but its schedule is not given in the main text.

protocols.name: ASCL1 + DLX2 programming (AD-iN cells)
protocols.principle: Transient expression of ASCL1 with DLX2 converts hPSCs in one step into an essentially pure GABAergic population with forebrain (ganglionic eminence) identity, reaching synaptic maturity in about five weeks without passing through a patterned progenitor.

source.authors: Yang N, Chanda S, Marro S, et al.
source.title: Generation of pure GABAergic neurons by transcription factor programming.

protocols.efficiency: 93.2 +/- 3.4% of cells MAP2+ at 4 weeks; with ASCL1+MYT1L+DLX2, 91.9 +/- 6.6% pan-DLX+, 81.4 +/- 4.7% GABA+ and 83.5 +/- 6.7% GAD67/65+; with ASCL1+DLX2 alone at 5 weeks, 93.5 +/- 2.7% FOXG1+, 89.1 +/- 3.5% GABA+ and 94.4 +/- 4.2% GAD65/67+; intrinsic properties indistinguishable across one ESC and three iPSC lines
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs in mTeSR1 dissociated with Accutase and plated on Matrigel-coated six-well plates with 2 uM thiazovivin on day -2 (H1 about 5 x 10^5, iPSC 7.5 x 10^5 cells per well).

stages.name: Plating and transduction

factors.name: Lentivirus: FUW-TetO-Ascl1-T2A-puro, FUW-TetO-Dlx2-IRES-hygro, FUW-rtTA
factors.conc: 1.5 uL per well of a six-well plate
factors.role: inducible ASCL1 and DLX2 with selection markers

stages.feeding: Fresh mTeSR1 with virus on day -1
actions: Plate dissociated hPSCs on Matrigel on day -2
Add lentivirus in fresh mTeSR1 on day -1
stages.checkpoint: Healthy attached cells before induction

stages.name: Transgene induction and selection

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.conc: 2 g/L as stated in the paper (i.e. 2 ug/mL)
factors.role: induces ASCL1 and DLX2; 14 days of doxycycline is enough for a stable neuronal fate

actions: Switch to N2 medium with doxycycline on day 0 and keep doxycycline for about two weeks
Run a 3-day drug selection from day 1
Plate mouse glia on Matrigel-coated coverslips on day 6
stages.checkpoint: Endogenous MYT1L, DLX1 and DLX5 induced around day 4; morphology comparable to the three-factor version by day 6

stages.name: Glia co-culture and maturation

factors.name: Ara-C
factors.conc: 2 g/L as stated in the paper, from about day 10

stages.feeding: Exchange 50% of the medium every 2-3 days
actions: Replate the iN cells onto the glia coverslips on day 7 (about 3 x 10^5 per well of a 24-well plate)
Assay at day 35 (5 weeks post-induction); DAPT improves neurite arborisation if desired
stages.checkpoint: Spontaneous and evoked IPSCs blocked by picrotoxin; SYN1/VGAT puncta on MAP2+ dendrites; both IPSC frequency and amplitude roughly double again by 7 weeks

tips: ASCL1 + DLX2 alone is sufficient; MYT1L mainly speeds up early morphological complexity, and endogenous MYT1L comes on by day 4 anyway.
Subtype markers come out in largely non-overlapping subpopulations: about 37% SST+, 28% calbindin+, 9% calretinin+ at 5 weeks, with ISL1 in roughly 20% and only a small fraction PV+.
14 days of doxycycline is enough for cell-fate stability: the grafted cells stay GABAergic and keep maturing in the mouse brain for 3 months without the transgene.
pitfalls: These are programmed rather than developmentally patterned neurons: the population spans MGE, LGE and CGE-like signatures plus olfactory bulb, striatal and prethalamic identities, so it is not a pure cortical interneuron model.
PV+ cells remain rare, and adding subtype transcription factors on top of ASCL1+DLX2 did not change the subtype mix.
CTIP2, NKX2-1, SP8 and DARPP-32 cells are essentially absent, so this is not a route to striatal projection neurons.
unverified: Puromycin and hygromycin concentrations are not stated in the methods text.
Doxycycline and Ara-C are quoted in the paper as 2 g/L; reproduced as printed.

cell_types.notes: Timing, not dose, is the control knob in directed differentiation: the same SHH concentration gives hypothalamic cells at days 2-18, cholinergic neurons at days 6-18, and MGE-like interneuron progenitors at days 10-18. Expect slow maturation - the companion paper (Nicholas CR, Chen J, Tang Y, et al., Cell Stem Cell 2013;12:573-86; PMID 23642366, doi 10.1016/j.stem.2013.04.005) found an intrinsic timeline of up to 7 months, and grafted precursors still look immature at 3 months. Mouse cortical feeders accelerate maturation noticeably more than human ones do, which is a confound to keep in mind when comparing papers. Transcription-factor programming (ASCL1+DLX2) gets to mature inhibitory synapses in about 5 weeks but produces a mixture of MGE-, LGE- and CGE-like identities plus olfactory bulb and prethalamic cells, so it is a GABAergic neuron model rather than a cortical interneuron model. PV+ neurons remain scarce in every published route.

cell_types.name: Astrocytes
cell_types.summary: The most abundant glial cell of the CNS, responsible for potassium and glutamate homeostasis, synaptogenesis, metabolic support and the inflammatory response, and regionally diverse. hPSC-derived astrocytes are used for neuron-glia co-culture, for APOE and other glial-autonomous disease mechanisms in Alzheimer's disease and ALS, and as a feeder layer that matures hPSC-derived neurons.
cell_types.maturation_note: Human gliogenesis is intrinsically late - the switch takes 6-9 months in vivo and 3-6 months in conventional culture. The three routes differ almost entirely in how they get past that: long neurosphere expansion (about 120 days), sparse seeding into a low-serum astrocyte medium (<30 days), or forcing NFIA, which confers glial competence in 5 days. Morphology keeps changing with passage, from large flat cells to long, complex processes.

morphology.endpoint: Flat, polygonal to stellate cells with large nuclei and several broad processes, growing as a loose monolayer with visible gaps. With passage and in co-culture they become more ramified, with long thin branches. Polygonal, piled-up, phase-dark cells usually mean a reactive phenotype from too much serum.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Standard compact colonies; some routes start instead from banked NPCs.

stages.label: Neuroepithelium and rosettes
stages.look: Radial rosettes; this is the window in which regional identity is set by RA or SHH.

stages.label: Expanding spheres
stages.look: Smooth free-floating aggregates; triturate weekly to suppress neurogenesis and avoid dark necrotic centres.

stages.label: Astroglial progenitors ('astrospheres')
stages.look: Spheres that re-form after dissociation and are now about 80% S100B+ and CD44+ but only about 10% GFAP+.

stages.label: Immature astrocytes
stages.look: Flat stellate cells plated sparsely on poly-ornithine/laminin; without laminin they attach but do not flatten, which makes staining hard to read.

stages.label: Mature astrocyte monolayer
stages.look: Large stellate S100B+/GFAP+ cells with long processes, non-proliferating in the absence of mitogens.

markers.name: S100B
markers.note: The more reliable of the two classic markers: about 80% at day 90 in astrospheres and ~90% at 30 days in the NPC/astrocyte-medium route. S100B+/GFAP-negative cells are immature rather than wrong.

markers.name: GFAP
markers.note: The marker everyone quotes and the more variable one, both in hPSC-derived and in primary astrocytes - about 10% at day 90 of astrosphere culture but >90% after day 120, and 82% at 30 days in the NPC route. Use a panel, not GFAP alone.

markers.name: CD44
markers.note: The key sortable marker of glial competence: 65% CD44+ after 10 days of NFIA, and the basis of live FACS enrichment before astrocyte differentiation.

markers.name: NFIA
markers.note: Must be transient: sustained high NFIA arrests cells in G1 and blocks GFAP even in the presence of LIF.

markers.name: SOX9
markers.note: Glial transcription factor; with NFIB it is the basis of the Canals programming route.

markers.name: AQP4
markers.note: Used as a knock-in reporter locus (AQP4-H2B-GFP) to time astrocyte appearance.

markers.name: SLC1A3
markers.note: Glutamate transporter; positive within 30 days in the NPC/astrocyte-medium route.

markers.name: SLC1A2
markers.note: The main adult glutamate transporter and a reasonable maturity readout.

markers.name: ALDH1L1
markers.note: Pan-astrocyte marker, less variable than GFAP.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: Neuronal contamination; should be absent after day 120 in astrosphere cultures, but the NPC-medium route retains low levels of neuronal transcripts.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Quality control for leftover neuroepithelium.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: Check with O4 that the glial output has not gone down the oligodendrocyte route.

markers.name: LCN2
markers.note: Reactive/A1-like marker, induced by serum within days - the reason low-serum protocols matter.

markers.name: IL6
markers.note: Dose-dependent secretion after 24 h of poly(I:C), LPS or amyloid-beta 42; the parent NPCs secrete none, which makes it a clean functional release test.

functional_assays: Spontaneous and glutamate/ATP/KCl-evoked calcium transients
Glutamate uptake
IL-6 and IL-8 secretion after poly(I:C), LPS or amyloid-beta 42
Phagocytosis of pHrodo-labelled myelin or zymosan
Enhancement of microglial phagocytosis by astrocyte-conditioned medium
Support of neuronal maturation in co-culture (synapsin-1 puncta, mEPSC frequency)
Protection against glutamate excitotoxicity
Electrophysiology: minimal sodium currents, no action potentials
qc: S100B+ >= 80-90% by flow (preferred over GFAP as the primary purity readout)
GFAP+ >= 80% where the protocol claims it, acknowledging high variability
No MAP2+ or TUJ1+ neurons and no O4+ oligodendrocytes
Non-reactive baseline: low LCN2/C3, with inducible IL-6 on stimulation
Calcium response to ATP or glutamate

protocols.name: Astrospheres: long-term neuroepithelial expansion to regional astrocytes
protocols.principle: Neuroepithelial clusters are patterned early (or left alone for dorsal forebrain identity), then expanded as free-floating spheres with EGF and FGF2 and triturated weekly to suppress neurogenesis; after about three months the spheres have switched to gliogenic and release of mitogens plus CNTF gives nearly pure astrocytes.

source.authors: Krencik R, Zhang SC
source.title: Directed differentiation of functional astroglial subtypes from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: At day 90 about 80% S100B+, about 80% CD44+ and about 10% GFAP+; from astrospheres cultured past day 120, nearly all cells are S100B+ and >90% are S100B+/GFAP+ within a week of mitogen withdrawal, with no neurons detectable
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC-derived neuroepithelial cells at day 10 of differentiation (columnar epithelium in every colony), generated from colonies with no sign of spontaneous differentiation. Base medium throughout is neural medium (DMEM/F12 + NEAA + N2 + heparin 2 ug/mL).

stages.name: Regional patterning of neuroepithelium (optional)
stages.feeding: Replace half the medium every 2-3 days
actions: Mechanically remove non-neural colonies that lack rosettes
Add morphogens from day 10 and keep them to day 21 for full patterning; omit them for dorsal telencephalic astrocytes
At day 15 lift the rosette-containing clusters with a pipette and transfer to T25 flasks (8 mL per flask)
stages.checkpoint: 3-10 clearly distinguishable rosettes per colony at day 15; clusters should not be broken into single cells

stages.name: Gliogenic switch
stages.feeding: Replace 75% of the medium every 2-3 days
actions: Add EGF and FGF2 from day 21; morphogens are no longer needed
Break large spheres weekly with a flame-polished Pasteur pipette (0.2-0.5 mm aperture) to suppress neurogenesis
Discard any spheres that attach firmly or form monolayers
stages.checkpoint: Day 90: 'astrospheres' that are ~80% S100B+ and ~80% CD44+; check that PAX6, MAP2 and O4 cells are absent

stages.name: Astroglial progenitor amplification
actions: Dissociate with Accutase (never trypsin) and replate at >=100,000 cells/mL in T25 flasks
Progenitors re-aggregate into new astrospheres; expand for 6-8 months in total if large numbers are needed
stages.checkpoint: Spheres re-form; rapidly dividing fibroblast-like cells that never re-form spheres mean a non-neural/neural-crest contamination

stages.name: Terminal differentiation

factors.name: CNTF
factors.role: activates gliogenic gene expression via JAK signalling

stages.feeding: Medium change every 2 days for 6 days
actions: Dissociate astrospheres to single cells and plate at 10,000 cells/cm2 on poly-L-ornithine/laminin coverslips
Let the cells attach for 3-5 h, then add neural medium with CNTF for 6 days
stages.checkpoint: Flat stellate S100B+/GFAP+ cells, no proliferation (no EGF/FGF2); glutamate uptake, calcium waves, minimal sodium currents and no action potentials

tips: Patterning has to happen at the neuroepithelial stage (days 10-21); after that the regional identity of the astrocytes is fixed. Unpatterned cultures default to dorsal telencephalic.
Without laminin the cells attach but do not flatten, which makes immunostaining hard to read; 1% serum for the first 24 h is an alternative way to get attachment.
Markers for astroglial progenitors are poor: S100B and CD44 come up before GFAP, and GFAP-negative/S100B-positive cells are immature rather than wrong.
pitfalls: Incomplete neural induction is the main failure: non-neural cells proliferate fast and take over.
Trypsin is not tolerated - the cells recover badly.
Replating below about 100,000 cells/mL stops astroglial progenitors proliferating.
Letting single spheres grow too large gives dark necrotic centres.

protocols.name: Commercial astrocyte medium on forebrain NPCs (<30 days)
protocols.principle: Rather than engineering the gliogenic switch, forebrain NPCs are seeded very sparsely into a low-serum astrocyte medium; this alone yields replicative, non-reactive astrocytes within 30 days and works across dozens of patient lines.

source.authors: TCW J, Wang M, Pimenova AA, et al.
source.title: An Efficient Platform for Astrocyte Differentiation from Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.

protocols.efficiency: Across 42 NPC lines from 30 individuals, an average of 90% S100B+ and 82% GFAP+ by flow cytometry at 30 days; transcriptomes cluster with primary human fetal astrocytes (r = 0.945) and read as non-reactive
protocols.start_requirements: Forebrain-patterned NPCs maintained at high density on Matrigel in NPC medium (DMEM/F12, 1x N2, 1x B27-RA, 1 mg/mL laminin, 20 ng/mL FGF2), split 1:3-1:4 weekly with Accutase and used at low passage. NPC quality is the main predictor of success.

stages.name: Sparse seeding into astrocyte medium
stages.base_medium: Commercial astrocyte medium with 2% FBS and astrocyte growth supplement (ScienCell 1801 in the paper)

factors.name: Fetal bovine serum
factors.role: minimal serum exposure; more serum pushes the cells reactive

actions: Dissociate NPCs to single cells and seed at 15,000 cells/cm2 on Matrigel - near-single-cell density is critical
Switch straight into astrocyte medium; no intermediate stage
stages.checkpoint: Astrocyte morphology within 10 days

stages.name: Astrocyte maturation
actions: Continue to day 30; the astrocytes are replicative, can be expanded for months and cryopreserved
stages.checkpoint: Star-shaped morphology by day 30; ~90% S100B+ / ~82% GFAP+ by flow; ALDH1L1, vimentin, GLAST and GLUT1 positive

materials: Commercial astrocyte medium with 2% FBS and growth supplement
DMEM/F12, N2, B27-RA, laminin, FGF2 (for NPC maintenance)
tips: Use S100B rather than GFAP to judge the population: GFAP is the more variable marker both here and in primary astrocytes. Better still, use a panel or transcriptomics.
A simple functional release test: these astrocytes secrete IL-6 (and IL-8) in a dose-dependent way after 24 h of poly(I:C), LPS or amyloid-beta 42, whereas the parent NPCs secrete nothing.
The real advantage is throughput - dozens of lines in parallel, expandable and freezable, which is what case-control studies need.
pitfalls: Some NPC lines only work from very low-passage stocks, and not necessarily on the first attempt.
Seeding too densely, or skipping the single-cell dissociation, blocks the transition.
The protocol relies on a proprietary commercial medium, so composition is not defined and lots vary; the authors screened 11 conditions and only two commercial media worked.
unverified: The medium is proprietary; the only defined component the paper gives is 1-2% FBS.
Regional identity varies between lines and is not controlled by this protocol.

protocols.name: NFIA forced expression: gliogenic switch in days, not months
protocols.principle: NFIA is the molecular switch for human glial competence. A transient pulse of NFIA makes neurogenic NSCs glial-competent (CD44+) in about five days, and NFIA then has to be withdrawn so that LIF can drive GFAP expression - sustained high NFIA arrests the cells in G1 and blocks differentiation.

source.authors: Tchieu J, Calder EL, Guttikonda SR, et al.
source.title: NFIA is a gliogenic switch enabling rapid derivation of functional human astrocytes from pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: From an inducible NFIA hPSC line: 65% CD44+ after 10 days of NFIA, then 42% GFAP+ after 15 days of LIF. In transduced long-term NSCs, >60% GFAP+ by 56 days and nearly 100% by 77 days. Regional (cortical vs spinal) astrocytes give GFAP+ cells by 6-7 days of differentiation
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC-derived NSCs (cortical by LSB+XAV939, or ventral spinal by LSB + 1 uM retinoic acid + 1 uM purmorphamine), maintained on poly-ornithine/laminin/fibronectin in N2 medium with 10 ng/mL FGF2, 10 ng/mL EGF and 1:1000 B27; plated at 3.5 x 10^5 cells/cm2 for transduction.

stages.name: NFIA induction
stages.base_medium: NSC medium (N2 + 10 ng/mL FGF2 + 10 ng/mL EGF + B27 1:1000)

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.role: induces FUW-tetO-NFIA (lentivirus or an inducible hPSC line)

actions: Transduce NSCs with tetO-NFIA and M2-rtTA lentivirus for 16-20 h, or use an inducible NFIA line
Add doxycycline and change medium daily; glial competence appears within 5 days
Detach with 0.05% trypsin and label for CD44
stages.checkpoint: CD44+ (65% from the inducible line after 10 days); NFIA lengthens G1 and raises CDKN1A (p21)

stages.name: NFIA withdrawal and astrocyte differentiation
stages.base_medium: Astrocyte induction medium: N2 + 10 ng/mL HB-EGF + 10 ng/mL LIF, no doxycycline

factors.name: LIF
factors.role: drives GFAP once NFIA has fallen; most efficient of the glial factors tested

stages.feeding: Weekly passaging for the first 4 weeks after sorting, then every other week
actions: FACS-sort live CD44+ cells and replate in astrocyte medium without doxycycline
Keep LIF for about 15 days
stages.checkpoint: GFAP+/S100B+ cells with complex processes, loss of Ki-67; transcriptome correlates with primary fetal astrocytes; robust calcium transients to KCl and ATP (stronger than commercial primary fetal astrocytes)

materials: FUW-tetO-NFIA and M2-rtTA lentivirus (or an inducible NFIA hPSC line)
tips: NFIA has to come back down: keeping doxycycline on blocks GFAP even with LIF. Titrating the doxycycline dose down also permits GFAP induction, which fits the G1-arrest mechanism.
Because the NSCs can be patterned first, you get region-matched astrocytes - useful for ALS (spinal) versus cortical disease models.
TGF-beta1 treatment of plain NSCs induces endogenous NFIA and eventually GFAP+ cells, but much less efficiently than forced NFIA, so it is not a drop-in substitute.

Canals I, Ginisty A, Quist E, et al., Nat Methods 2018;15:693-696 (PMID 30127505, doi 10.1038/s41592-018-0103-2) is the main alternative transcription-factor route: SOX9 plus NFIB overexpressed in hPSCs gives homogeneous induced astrocytes with adult-like properties.
pitfalls: Success depends on how well the NSCs are transduced; an inducible line avoids that variable.
The pulse is reversible - remove doxycycline and keep the cells in NSC medium and they revert to a neurogenic state and lose glial competence.
Glial-competent cells migrate extensively along white matter after grafting, which is a feature for some experiments and a confound for others.

cell_types.notes: Pick the route by what the experiment needs. The astrosphere protocol is slow (about 4 months) but gives regionally specified, functionally characterised astrocytes and progenitors that expand for 6-8 months. The NPC-plus-commercial-medium route is fast and scales to dozens of patient lines, which is what case-control studies need, but relies on a proprietary medium and does not control regional identity. Forced NFIA gives glial competence in 5 days and, because the NSCs can be patterned first, region-matched astrocytes - at the cost of a transgene and a mandatory withdrawal step. GFAP is a genuinely unreliable single marker; use S100B plus a panel or transcriptomics. Serum is the main lever on reactivity: keep it at 1-2% or omit it, and treat a polygonal, piled-up morphology as a warning.

cell_types.name: Oligodendrocytes and OPCs
cell_types.summary: The myelinating glia of the CNS, derived through the OLIG2+ pMN domain and defined operationally by live O4 surface staining and then by MBP. They are used for multiple sclerosis and leukodystrophy modelling, for remyelination screens, and for the trophic support of axons that fails in ALS.
cell_types.maturation_note: The small-molecule route takes 75 days to O4+ OPCs and a further 3 weeks of growth-factor withdrawal for MBP+ oligodendrocytes. Transcription-factor routes compress this dramatically: SOX10 alone gives O4+ cells by day 22 (and about 89% by day 15 from a single-copy inducible line), with MBP+ cells from day 7 of induction. Myelination in co-culture takes about 20 further days.

morphology.endpoint: Small, phase-dark cell bodies with dense, highly branched processes that spread into flat membrane sheets; mature cells look almost web-like. O4 live staining is the practical way to find them, because the morphology overlaps with other glia early on.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Seeded sparsely (10,000 cells/cm2 in the Douvaras protocol) for adherent induction.

stages.label: OLIG2+ progenitors
stages.look: Multilayered dense structures; PAX6+ at day 7 then OLIG2+ by day 12.

stages.label: Spheres
stages.look: Smooth free-floating aggregates (at least 100 cells each) in which the OLIG2+ population is enriched.

stages.label: Early O4+ OPCs
stages.look: Cells migrating out of plated spheres, beginning to show the characteristic fine ramified processes.

stages.label: Late O4+ OPCs
stages.look: Small bodies with dense, highly branched processes; O4 live staining is strongly positive and these cells no longer divide.

stages.label: Mature oligodendrocytes
stages.look: Flat membrane sheets and highly branched processes, MBP positive, wrapping axons in co-culture.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Appears by day 7 of adherent induction with retinoic acid.

markers.name: OLIG2
markers.note: 70.1% at day 12 with SAG, 57.7% with recombinant SHH, 40.6% with retinoic acid alone. Day-12 OLIG2 predicts the final MBP yield, so it is the stage to optimise.

markers.name: NKX2-2
markers.note: Co-expressed with OLIG2 in cells committing to the oligodendrocyte lineage - the opposite of its meaning in motor neuron protocols, where it is a contaminant.

markers.name: SOX10
markers.note: The master regulator and the single sufficient programming factor; 97 +/- 8% of SOX10+ cells are also O4+.

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Early OPC marker that most O4+ cells have lost by day 75. Notably absent in SOX10-programmed cultures, which appear to skip the OPC stage - so do not use it as a checkpoint there.

markers.name: CSPG4
markers.note: Retained in day-75 O4+ cells after PDGFRA is lost; also retained in OPCs after grafting.

markers.name: O4 antigen
markers.alias: O4 sulfatide (not a gene product; antibody-defined)
markers.note: The operational purity readout and the basis for live staining and FACS. O4+ cells are post-mitotic (Ki-67 negative) while surrounding progenitors still divide.

markers.name: MBP
markers.note: 34 +/- 4% of O4+ cells after >=3 weeks of growth-factor withdrawal in the small-molecule route; about 10-21% of cells at day 22 in SOX10 programming. All MBP+ cells are post-mitotic.

markers.name: PLP1
markers.note: 20 +/- 3% of SOX10-induced cells, rising to about 95% of O4-purified cells.

markers.name: MOG
markers.note: Co-expressed in about 72% of MBP+ cells.

markers.name: MKI67
markers.note: 40-50% of progenitors are Ki-67+ during OPC expansion; O4+ and MBP+ cells must be negative.

markers.name: GFAP
markers.note: About 15% of cells in the small-molecule route; absent in SOX10-programmed cultures.

markers.name: MAP2
markers.note: About 20% of cells in the small-molecule route; under 5% in SOX10 programming.

markers.name: PMP22
markers.note: Worth checking because SOX10 also drives Schwann cell fate; no PMP22+ cells were found in the hPSC oligodendrocyte cultures.

functional_assays: Live O4 surface staining and FACS purification (cells freeze and thaw without losing morphology)
Myelination of hPSC-derived cortical neurons in co-culture (MBP sheaths wrapping TUJ1+ axons)
Myelination in shiverer mouse brain slices or after neonatal transplantation
Electron microscopy for compact multilayer myelin and g-ratio
96/384-well MBP-area myelination screens (T3, clobetasol, miconazole, pranlukast as positive controls)
qc: OLIG2+ >= 60-70% at day 12 as the gate on the whole run
O4+ >= 50% by live staining or flow at the endpoint (day 75 small-molecule, day 22 SOX10)
MBP+ cells present and Ki-67 negative after growth factor withdrawal
No PMP22+ Schwann cells
Astrocyte (GFAP) and neuronal (TUJ1) fractions quantified, or sorted away

protocols.name: Adherent dual SMAD inhibition with low-dose retinoid: O4+ OPCs by day 75
protocols.principle: Starting retinoic acid at day 0 together with dual SMAD inhibition, then adding a smoothened agonist from day 8, recapitulates the pMN domain of the spinal cord and gives a large OLIG2+ population by day 12; aggregating the cells into spheres then enriches that population and restricts it to the oligodendrocyte lineage.

source.authors: Douvaras P, Wang J, Zimmer M, et al.
source.title: Efficient generation of myelinating oligodendrocytes from primary progressive multiple sclerosis patients by induced pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: 70.1% OLIG2+ at day 12 with SAG; up to 70% O4+ cells at day 75 from the RUES1 hESC line and 43.6-62.1% from four PPMS patient iPSC lines; 34 +/- 4% of O4+ OPCs become MBP+ after >=3 weeks of growth factor withdrawal. Residual cultures are about 15% GFAP+ and 20% MAP2+
protocols.start_requirements: hESC/hiPSC plated at 10,000 cells/cm2 at day 0 in adherent (not suspension) culture for dual SMAD inhibition.

stages.name: Caudalised neural induction

factors.name: all-trans retinoic acid
factors.role: caudalisation from day 0; about 100-fold lower than the dose most groups use, and it upregulates OLIG2 even without exogenous SHH

actions: Plate at only 10,000 cells/cm2 at day 0 and induce adherently
Keep retinoic acid from the very start
stages.checkpoint: PAX6+ cells by day 7

stages.name: Ventralisation to OLIG2+ progenitors

factors.name: SAG (smoothened agonist)
factors.role: ventralisation; more effective here than 100 ng/mL recombinant SHH

actions: Add SAG at day 8
stages.checkpoint: Multilayered structures by day 12; 70.1% OLIG2+ (vs 57.7% with recombinant SHH, 40.6% with RA alone)

stages.name: Sphere aggregation
stages.base_medium: Neural medium with retinoic acid and SAG, low-attachment plates
actions: Lift adherent cells at day 12 and seed into low-attachment plates to form spheres
Note that at least 100 cells are needed per sphere
stages.checkpoint: Only OLIG2-GFP+ cells form aggregates, so the aggregation step itself enriches the OLIG2 population

stages.name: OPC expansion
stages.base_medium: PDGF medium, on poly-L-ornithine/laminin from day 30
actions: Add PDGF-AA, HGF, IGF-1 and NT-3 from day 20
Plate spheres onto poly-L-ornithine/laminin at day 30 and let cells migrate out
Live-stain with O4 antibody from about day 50; the population rises sharply around day 75
FACS-purify O4+ cells; they freeze and thaw without losing morphology
stages.checkpoint: Highly ramified O4+ cells co-expressing OLIG2, SOX10 and NG2; O4+ cells are non-dividing while 40-50% of the remaining progenitors are Ki-67+

stages.name: Oligodendrocyte maturation
stages.feeding: Per schedule for at least 3 weeks
actions: Withdraw growth factors and keep for >=3 weeks
stages.checkpoint: 34 +/- 4% MBP+ mature oligodendrocytes; in vivo, compact myelin with major dense and intraperiod lines and about 31% of host axons ensheathed at 16 weeks in shiverer mice

tips: The step-by-step version is Douvaras P, Fossati V, Nat Protoc 2015;10:1143-54 (PMID 26134954, doi 10.1038/nprot.2015.075).
Retinoid dose is the counter-intuitive part: 100 nM, roughly a hundredth of the dose commonly used, gave the best OLIG2 yields, and worked even without exogenous SHH by inducing endogenous SHH.
SAG outperformed recombinant SHH and is cheaper.
By day 75 most O4+ cells have lost PDGFRA but keep NG2, so do not expect PDGFRA to mark late OPCs.
pitfalls: 75 days is still a long run, and the culture is never pure - expect roughly 15% astrocytes and 20% neurons alongside the OPCs unless you sort.
Spheres smaller than about 100 cells do not form.
Line-to-line variation is real: 44-70% O4+ across six lines.
unverified: Concentrations of PDGF-AA, HGF, IGF-1 and NT-3 and the exact dual-SMAD inhibitor doses are in the supplementary media tables, which were not retrievable.
Day boundaries for the PDGF medium overlap the sphere stage in the source (growth factors from day 20 while spheres run to day 30); represented here as overlapping stages.

protocols.name: SOX10 alone: O4+ oligodendrocytes in about 22 days
protocols.principle: Overexpressing the single transcription factor SOX10 in caudalised, ventralised neural precursors is enough to drive them to O4+ and MBP+ oligodendrocytes in about ten days, skipping the intermediate OPC stage; SOX10 cannot do this in uncommitted hPSCs.

source.authors: Garcia-Leon JA, Kumar M, Boon R, et al.
source.title: SOX10 Single Transcription Factor-Based Fast and Efficient Generation of Oligodendrocytes from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells.

protocols.efficiency: Lentiviral SOX10 in day-12 NPCs: 54.05 +/- 2.52% O4+ at day 22, with 97.15 +/- 8.19% of SOX10+ cells also O4+ and 21.48 +/- 2.09% of SOX10+ cells MBP+; across eight lines (including two PPMS and two familial ALS iPSC lines) 50-65% O4+ and about 10% MBP+ at day 22. A single-copy doxycycline-inducible SOX10 line at the AAVS1 locus reaches 89.3 +/- 0.6% O4+ by day 15
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs dissociated to single cells two days before day 0; neural induction is run in N2B27 medium. The NPCs must already be caudal/ventral (OLIG2-competent) - SOX10 in naive hPSCs gives no oligodendrocytes.

stages.name: Caudalised, ventralised neural induction

factors.name: Smoothened agonist
factors.role: ventralisation, added day 8 after the SMAD inhibitors are withdrawn

actions: Dissociate hPSCs at day -2; start N2B27 with SB431542, LDN-193189 and retinoic acid at day 0
Withdraw SB431542 and LDN-193189 at day 8 and add the smoothened agonist
Dissociate and replate at day 12 for transduction
stages.checkpoint: Day 12: >95% SOX2+/nestin+, 81.8 +/- 2.7% HOXB4+ and about 52% OLIG2+ but no O4

stages.name: SOX10 induction and oligodendrocyte differentiation

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.role: induces TetO-SOX10 from the day after transduction

actions: Transduce the day-12 NPCs with inducible SOX10 lentivirus (or use an AAVS1 SOX10 line and simply add doxycycline at day 8)
Add doxycycline the next day in oligodendrocyte differentiation medium
Maintain 7-10 days; FACS-purify O4+ cells if required - they cryopreserve with >90% viability
stages.checkpoint: Day 22: ~50-60% O4+ and O1+, highly branched with membrane sheaths; MBP+ cells are Ki-67 negative; no GFAP+ astrocytes, <5% TUJ1+ neurons and no PMP22+ Schwann cells

stages.name: Myelination co-culture (optional)

factors.name: Doxycycline
factors.role: kept during co-culture, though SOX10 is no longer required for maturation

factors.name: Triiodothyronine (T3)
factors.role: pro-myelinating; withdrawn in the screening format so drug effects can be read

actions: Seed purified O4+ cells onto hPSC-derived cortical neurons that have matured 10-14 days
Culture 20 days; scales to 96- and 384-well plates for myelination screens
stages.checkpoint: MBP+ sheaths aligned with and wrapping TUJ1+ axons, confirmed as multilayer compact myelin by electron microscopy

materials: Inducible SOX10 lentivirus (or an AAVS1 inducible SOX10 line)
tips: SOX8 and SOX9 also induce O4 (37-50%) but SOX10 is the best single factor, and adding any of the other five candidate factors to SOX10 gave no further improvement.
No PDGFRA+ or NG2+ cells appear, which suggests SOX10 generates late OPCs/oligodendrocytes directly without an intermediate OPC stage - do not screen for NG2 as a checkpoint.
The single-copy AAVS1 line removes random-integration and transduction-efficiency variability and is the better option for screening.
In the authors' own screen, clobetasol gave the biggest increase in MBP (3-4 fold over DMSO, more than T3), pranlukast 1.5-2.5 fold and miconazole about as much as T3, while DAPT gave no increase.
pitfalls: SOX10 in uncommitted hPSCs produces nothing - the NPC stage and its OLIG2 competence are essential.
Lentiviral delivery leaves about 24% Ki-67+ cells in the culture at day 22 (the MBP+ cells themselves are post-mitotic).
Lines differ: one iPSC line with lower day-12 OLIG2 (30.7% vs 51.7%) gave correspondingly fewer MBP+ cells.
unverified: T3 concentration in the co-culture medium is not stated in the available text.
Composition of the oligodendrocyte differentiation and co-culture media is in the supplementary experimental procedures, which were not retrievable.

Ehrlich M, Mozafari S, Glatza M, et al., PNAS 2017;114:E2243-E2252 (PMID 28246330, doi 10.1073/pnas.1614412114) reports up to 70% O4+ in 28 days with SOX10 + OLIG2 + NKX6.2; its stage concentrations could not be verified because the PMC record returned no full text.

cell_types.notes: Two surprises in the small-molecule literature are worth knowing. First, the useful retinoic acid dose is about a hundred times lower than most groups had been using (100 nM), and at that dose RA alone induces OLIG2 by raising endogenous SHH. Second, SAG outperforms recombinant SHH and is far cheaper. Transcription-factor routes have largely displaced the 100+ day protocols for screening work: SOX10 alone suffices (Garcia-Leon), while Ehrlich M, Mozafari S, Glatza M, et al., PNAS 2017;114:E2243-E2252 (PMID 28246330, doi 10.1073/pnas.1614412114) reported up to 70% O4+ in 28 days with SOX10 + OLIG2 + NKX6.2; the difference is probably in how the starting NPCs were made. Neither route makes a pure culture without sorting on O4, and MBP+ fractions stay well below the O4+ fraction in every protocol.

cell_types.name: Cerebral (brain) organoids
cell_types.summary: Self-organising 3D tissues that reproduce the cytoarchitecture of the developing human cortex - ventricle-like lumens, a ventricular and subventricular zone, inner and outer radial glia, and layered projection neurons - and later astrocytes. They are used for human-specific neurodevelopment, microcephaly and other developmental disorders, and for questions that need tissue-level organisation.
cell_types.maturation_note: SOX2/PAX6 neuroepithelium by day 12-20, neurons from one month, multiple brain regions and layer identities by 2-3 months, astrocytes and inhibitory precursors by 6 months. Cortical spheroids map transcriptionally to 19-24 post-conception weeks at 2.5 months. Progenitor zones disappear by 5-6 months and self-patterned organoids then start to shrink.

morphology.endpoint: An opaque sphere of a few millimetres with translucent lobes at the surface. In section, rosette-like ventricular zones with bright lumens are ringed by a dense neuronal mantle; pigmented patches mark retinal tissue in self-patterned organoids.

stages.label: Embryoid bodies
stages.look: 9,000 cells per well in a U- or V-bottom low-attachment plate; dead cells around the aggregate on day 1 are normal.

stages.label: Brightened EBs
stages.look: 500-600 um aggregates with smooth edges and a translucent surface - the signal to move to induction medium.

stages.label: Neuroepithelium on the EB surface
stages.look: Radially organised, optically translucent pseudostratified tissue around the outside of the aggregate.

stages.label: Neuroepithelial buds
stages.look: Large continuous epithelial buds with fluid-filled, ventricle-like cavities protruding from the Matrigel droplet; migratory fibroblast-like cells spread into the gel.

stages.label: Expanded cortical tissue
stages.look: A millimetre-scale organoid too large for a standard tissue-culture scope; neuroepithelial loops with a dense neuronal mantle, visible only in section.

stages.label: Mature organoid with glia
stages.look: Progenitor zones have shrunk away; tissue is mostly neurons with S100B+/GFAP+ astrocytes threaded through the neuropil.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Inner radial glia inside the ventricular zone and outer radial glia beyond it; both phospho-vimentin+ in mitosis but dividing at different positions.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Expressed in 100% of dorsally patterned organoids at 1, 3 and 6 months; >85% of cells at day 18 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: FOXG1
markers.note: Forebrain identity; in self-patterned organoids it marks the forebrain region among several.

markers.name: EMX1
markers.note: Dorsal identity; 89% of dorsally patterned organoids across lines and timepoints.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Defines a subventricular-zone-like rim around each ventricular zone.

markers.name: HOPX
markers.note: Outer radial glia, the progenitor type expanded in human cortex; present in dorsally patterned organoids from 3 months.

markers.name: TBR1
markers.note: Peaks at about 41% of cells at day 76 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: BCL11B
markers.note: Expressed by 3 months and maintained; only about 3% of cells co-express CTIP2 and SATB2, as expected.

markers.name: SATB2
markers.note: Upper-layer identity; rises up to 7-fold from day 52 to day 137 and is the honest test of culture duration.

markers.name: S100B
markers.note: Astrocytes are genuinely late: 2.7% GFAP+ at day 35, about 8% at day 76 and almost 20% at day 180 in cortical spheroids.

markers.name: GFAP
markers.note: Early on it marks radial glial processes inside the ventricular zone rather than astrocytes - read it together with position and morphology.

markers.name: TTR
markers.note: A normal region of self-patterned organoids (highly convoluted cuboidal epithelium) but an unwanted identity in a dorsally patterned preparation.

markers.name: NKX2-1
markers.note: Present in self-patterned organoids; should be minimal under dorsal patterning.

markers.name: MKI67
markers.note: Positive in all 3-month organoids tested; its disappearance by 5-6 months marks the end of neurogenesis.

functional_assays: Acute slice patch clamp with extracellular stimulation (EPSPs and spike firing)
Calcium imaging of intact or sliced organoids (Fluo-4, Fura-2)
Single-cell RNA-seq with intraclass correlation or mutual information for reproducibility
Array tomography and electron microscopy for synapses and glycogen granules
EdU/BrdU birthdating for the order of layer genesis
Live imaging of interkinetic nuclear migration in radial glia
qc: EBs 500-600 um, brightened with smooth edges before neural induction
Radially organised neuroepithelium before Matrigel embedding
PAX6 and MAP2 positive in essentially all organoids by 1-3 months; EMX1 positive for dorsal patterning
CTIP2 and SATB2 present by 3 months
Control organoids from the same batch and medium analysed alongside every experimental group
Low cleaved caspase-3 and low hypoxia signature in the core

protocols.name: Self-patterned cerebral organoids (Matrigel droplet + agitation)
protocols.principle: Embryoid bodies are given a minimal neural induction medium that will not support mesoderm or endoderm, then embedded in a Matrigel droplet that provides the missing basement membrane so continuous, correctly oriented neuroepithelium can bud out; agitation then supplies enough oxygen and nutrients for the tissue to grow into multiple brain regions without added patterning factors.

source.authors: Lancaster MA, Knoblich JA
source.title: Generation of cerebral organoids from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: If EBs clear and brighten properly, 60-80% go on to show neuroectoderm; neuroepithelial buds then form in 30-80% of organoids. Batch-to-batch variability is substantial and is the protocol's main limitation
protocols.start_requirements: hESC or iPSC colonies, feeder-dependent or feeder-free, 70-80% confluent in one well of a 6-well plate with no more than 5-10% differentiation and clear colony borders. One well yields roughly a 96-well plate of EBs.

stages.name: Embryoid body formation
stages.base_medium: Low-bFGF hESC medium (DMEM/F12, 20% knockout serum replacement, 3% hESC-quality FBS, GlutaMAX, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol)

factors.name: bFGF (FGF2)
factors.role: low FGF2 for the first ~4 days

factors.name: Y-27632 (ROCK inhibitor)
factors.role: limits cell death during aggregation; first ~4 days only

stages.feeding: Replace about half the medium every other day (add 150 uL fresh)
actions: Dissociate to single cells, resuspend in low-bFGF medium with ROCK inhibitor and plate 9,000 live cells in 150 uL per well of a 96-well ultra-low-attachment U-bottom plate
Keep ROCK inhibitor and low bFGF only until the EBs brighten or exceed 350-400 um
Feed with plain hESC medium (no ROCK inhibitor, no bFGF) while EBs are 350-600 um
stages.checkpoint: By day 5-6 EBs are 500-600 um, brightening, with smooth edges and optically translucent surface tissue

stages.name: Neural induction
stages.base_medium: Neural induction medium: DMEM/F12 + 1% N2 + 1% GlutaMAX + 1% NEAA + 1 ug/mL heparin
stages.feeding: Add another 500 uL of induction medium 48 h after transfer
actions: Transfer each EB with a cut 200 uL tip (1-1.5 mm opening) into 500 uL of neural induction medium in a low-attachment 24-well plate
Never scoop EBs with a spatula - it damages them
stages.checkpoint: After 4-5 days the outer surface shows radially organised pseudostratified neuroepithelium; move to Matrigel promptly, late transfer compromises later morphology

stages.name: Matrigel embedding and static culture
stages.base_medium: Cerebral organoid differentiation medium (1:1 DMEM/F12 : Neurobasal, 0.5% N2, 1:4000 insulin, GlutaMAX, NEAA, 1:100 B27 without vitamin A, 3.5 uL/L 2-mercaptoethanol, pen/strep)

factors.name: B27 without vitamin A
factors.role: no retinoid at this stage, to avoid caudalising the tissue

stages.feeding: Feed at 48 h; full medium change by tilting the dish and letting droplets settle
actions: Make a 4x4 grid of dimples in Parafilm, transfer one tissue per dimple with a cut 200 uL tip, remove excess medium and drip about 30 uL Matrigel over each
Centre the tissue in the droplet with a 10 uL tip before the Matrigel sets, then polymerise 20-30 min at 37 C
Add 5 mL differentiation medium (no vitamin A) and shake the droplets off the Parafilm
Keep static for 4 days
stages.checkpoint: Within 1-3 days, buds of expanded neuroepithelium with fluid-filled cavities; migratory fibroblast-like cells spreading into the Matrigel are normal and seem to help budding

stages.name: Agitated growth and regional diversification
stages.base_medium: Cerebral organoid differentiation medium with B27 containing vitamin A
stages.feeding: Full medium change every 3-4 days on a shaker, or weekly in a spinner flask
actions: Transfer embedded organoids with a cut 1 mL tip (about 3 mm opening) to a 125 mL spinning bioreactor in 75-100 mL medium, or to an orbital shaker at 85 rpm
Do not put more than 32 organoids in one 125 mL flask or they fuse
Section and immunostain rather than trying to image whole organoids after day 15-20
stages.checkpoint: Day 12-20: SOX2/PAX6 neuroepithelium around ventricle-like cavities. From one month: TUJ1/DCX neurons, FOXG1 forebrain, TTR choroid plexus, PROX1/FZD9 hippocampus, NKX2-1 ventral forebrain, pigmented retina; inner and outer radial glia (both SOX2+, phospho-vimentin+ in mitosis) dividing at different positions; TBR2 intermediate progenitors; RELN/TBR1 preplate

materials: N2, B27 (with and without vitamin A)
tips: Three timing decisions make or break a batch: start only from colonies with optimal morphology, move EBs to induction medium at the right size and brightness, and get the tissues into Matrigel as soon as radial organisation appears.
An orbital shaker is a practical substitute for the spinner flask and lets many conditions run in parallel; the authors saw no morphological difference.
Progenitor zones shrink and disappear by 5-6 months and organoids then start shrinking after 6-7 months, though they can be kept over a year.
Non-radial translucent buds are not ideal but usually do not ruin the organoid, as long as radial organisation is present somewhere.
pitfalls: Variability between preparations is large, so a phenotype must be robust enough to sit outside the normal range; always grow control organoids in the same batch and the same medium.
No meninges and no vasculature, which caps growth and gives necrotic cores without agitation.
Regional identity is self-patterned and stochastic - a given organoid may be mostly non-forebrain (see Velasco 2019 for the quantified comparison).
Six-layer cortical architecture is never achieved; only a rudimentary deep/superficial split.
unverified: 2-mercaptoethanol is added as 87.5 uL of a 1:100 dilution per 250 mL; final molarity not stated.
The source gives the whole-organoid culture period as open-ended (up to a year); 60 days is used here as the typical analysis window.

protocols.name: Human cortical spheroids (hCS) - no scaffold, no replating
protocols.principle: Intact hPSC colonies are lifted into suspension, neuralised with dorsomorphin and SB431542, then expanded with FGF2 and EGF; the long mitogen exposure lets the progenitors run through neurogenesis and then switch to gliogenesis, so the spheroids end up with laminated cortical neurons and non-reactive astrocytes from the same genetic background, in a form thin enough to slice and patch.

source.authors: Pasca AM, Sloan SA, Clarke LE, et al.
source.title: Functional cortical neurons and astrocytes from human pluripotent stem cells in 3D culture.

protocols.efficiency: By day 18, over 85% of cells PAX6+ and more than 80% of those FOXG1+; at ~7 weeks 78.8 +/- 2.5% TUBB3+ and 36.2 +/- 3.6% NEUN+; GFAP+ cells 2.7 +/- 0.7% at day 35, about 8% at day 76 and almost 20% at day 180; reproducible across seven iPSC lines from five subjects
protocols.start_requirements: hiPSCs grown on inactivated DR4 mouse embryonic fibroblast feeders; intact colonies are detached with low-concentration dispase (0.7 mg/mL) for about 30 min - not dissociated to single cells.

stages.name: Spheroid formation and neural induction
stages.base_medium: hiPSC medium without FGF2 (DMEM/F12 with 20% knockout serum, NEAA, GlutaMAX, 0.1 nM 2-mercaptoethanol)
actions: Transfer the detached colonies into ultra-low-attachment 100 mm plates; they fold into spheres within hours
Give both SMAD inhibitors for the first five days
stages.checkpoint: Uniform floating spheroids

stages.name: Progenitor expansion
stages.base_medium: Neural medium: Neurobasal + B27 without vitamin A + GlutaMAX + pen/strep

factors.name: EGF
factors.role: progenitor expansion; the long exposure is what later drives the gliogenic switch

stages.feeding: Daily for the first 10 days, then every other day for 9 days
actions: Move the spheroids to neural medium with FGF2 and EGF on day 6
stages.checkpoint: Day 18: >85% PAX6+, >80% FOXG1+; spheroids >300 um by two weeks

stages.name: Neuronal differentiation
actions: Swap FGF2/EGF for BDNF and NT-3 on day 25
stages.checkpoint: Ventricular-zone-like rosettes around N-cadherin+ lumens with a TBR2+ SVZ-like rim; PAX6+ radial glia with GFAP+ processes and interkinetic nuclear migration

stages.name: Maturation, lamination and astrogenesis
stages.base_medium: Neural medium only, no growth factors
actions: From day 43 use plain neural medium; spheroids reach up to 4 mm by 2.5 months and can be kept 9 months
Slice to 250 um for acute recordings, or dissociate for monolayer work
stages.checkpoint: TBR1 peaks at ~40.7% of cells at day 76; superficial markers (SATB2, BRN2, CUX1/2) rise up to 7-fold from day 52 to 137 and end roughly equal to deep layers; neurons laminate concentrically around the ventricular zone; 88.8% show spontaneous synaptic activity abolished by NBQX+D-AP5

tips: Transcriptionally these spheroids map to the late mid-fetal human cortex (19-24 post-conception weeks) at 2.5 months, later than 2D monolayer or other 3D methods.

Astrocytes arise spontaneously - no CNTF, LIF or serum - which is why they read as non-reactive. Adding serum flips them to a reactive, polygonal phenotype with LCN2 and other reactive transcripts up.
The method is deliberately simple: no replating, no Matrigel embedding, no bioreactor; just low-attachment plates with twice-weekly medium changes.
Only dorsal telencephalic excitatory neurons are made - there are no interneurons here either.
pitfalls: Starting from single cells instead of intact colonies changes the method; the colony-lifting step is part of the design.
Superficial-layer neurons only reach parity with deep layers after months; ending at day 52 gives a deep-layer-biased culture.
Daily medium changes for the first 10 days are labour-intensive and are where contamination creeps in.
unverified: Y-27632 concentration for the first 24 h is not stated in the methods.

protocols.name: Dorsally patterned forebrain organoids (reproducible cell diversity)
protocols.principle: Rather than letting organoids pattern themselves, WNT and TGF-beta are inhibited for the first 18 days to fix a dorsal forebrain identity; adapted to spinner-flask bioreactors, this gives large organoids whose cell-type composition is as reproducible between organoids as between individual human or mouse brains.

source.authors: Velasco S, Kedaigle AJ, Simmons SK, et al.
source.title: Individual brain organoids reproducibly form cell diversity of the human cerebral cortex.

protocols.efficiency: About 90% efficiency of forebrain cell-type generation (93/103 organoids); 95% of 21 organoids profiled by single-cell RNA-seq gave a near-indistinguishable set of cell types; 100% expressed PAX6 and MAP2 at 1, 3 and 6 months, 89% also EMX1; intraclass correlation of cell-type proportions 0.85 at 3 months versus 0.39 for self-patterned whole-brain organoids
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free hPSCs on Geltrex in mTeSR1, 80-90% confluent, below passage 50, mycoplasma-negative, karyotypically normal, with tightly packed round cells and large nucleoli.

stages.name: Aggregation and dorsal patterning
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium I: Glasgow-MEM, 20% knockout serum replacement, 0.1 mM MEM-NEAA, 1 mM pyruvate, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, pen/strep

factors.name: IWR1
factors.role: WNT inhibitor; holds dorsal forebrain identity, days 0-18

actions: Dissociate to single cells with Accutase and reaggregate 9,000 cells per well in ultra-low-adhesion V-bottom 96-well plates on day 0
Keep Y-27632 to day 6 and IWR1 + SB431542 to day 18
stages.checkpoint: By one month, EMX1+/PAX6+ dorsalised progenitors lining ventricle-like cavities with MAP2+ neurons

stages.name: Orbital agitation
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium II: DMEM/F12, 2 mM GlutaMAX, 1% N2, 1% chemically defined lipid concentrate, 0.25 ug/mL fungizone, pen/strep
actions: Move the aggregates to ultra-low-attachment dishes under orbital agitation at 70 rpm on day 18
stages.checkpoint: Consistent, roughly spherical aggregates

stages.name: Bioreactor growth
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium III: CDM II + 10% FBS + 5 ug/mL heparin + 1% Matrigel

factors.name: Matrigel
factors.role: soluble extracellular matrix; avoids the need for droplet embedding

actions: Transfer to spinner-flask bioreactors at 56 rpm on day 35; this removes the need for 40% O2, bisecting the aggregates, or high-oxygen-permeability dishes
stages.checkpoint: By 3 months, CTIP2+ and SATB2+ cortical projection neurons, FOXG1, HOPX+ outer radial glia, TBR1, TBR2/EOMES, Reelin; VGluT1/PSD95 co-localisation indicating excitatory synapses

stages.name: Long-term culture and astrogenesis
stages.base_medium: Cortical Differentiation Medium IV: CDM III + B27 supplement + 2% Matrigel
actions: Switch to CDM IV from day 70 and maintain at least 6 months
stages.checkpoint: At 6 months, substantial S100B+/GFAP+ astrocytes plus cycling and immature inhibitory interneuron precursors; markers of apoptosis and hypoxia stay low

tips: If you need quantitative, organoid-to-organoid comparisons, this patterned model is the one with the published reproducibility numbers; the self-patterned whole-brain model gave forebrain cells in only 4 of 19 organoids in the same study.
Exogenous patterning does not cost you fidelity: dorsally patterned and self-patterned organoids correlated equally well (0.67-0.80) with human fetal cortex cells.
Three months is already enough for most neurodevelopmental questions; six months is needed for astrocytes and later-born types.
Reproducibility held across five stem cell lines, three independent batches and both sexes.
pitfalls: Starting material quality is explicitly the gate: below passage 50, mycoplasma-free, normal karyotype, 80-90% confluent with undifferentiated morphology.
Occasional organoids stall - one of 12 at six months expressed no neuronal markers at all and had to be excluded.
The protocol consumes many lots of FBS, KSR and Matrigel over a long differentiation (13, 4 and 23 lots respectively in this study), so lot variability has to be tracked.
unverified: This is a modification of Kadoshima et al.; the B27 concentration in CDM IV is not numerically stated in the methods.

cell_types.notes: Reproducibility is the issue that separates these protocols, and it has been measured. Self-patterned whole-brain organoids had an intraclass correlation of cell-type proportions of 0.39, with only 4 of 19 organoids generating substantial forebrain; dorsally patterned forebrain organoids scored 0.85 at 3 months, with organoid-to-organoid variation comparable to that between individual human or mouse brains. If you need quantitative comparisons, pattern the organoids. Self-patterning is still the right choice when you want multiple interacting regions (choroid plexus, hippocampus, retina) in one tissue. All three models lack vasculature and meninges, which caps growth and is why agitation is non-negotiable, and none achieves six-layer cortical architecture.

cell_types.name: Brain microvascular endothelial-like cells (blood-brain barrier model)
cell_types.summary: Cells that reproduce the defining functions of the blood-brain barrier: continuous tight junctions with very high transendothelial electrical resistance, BBB nutrient transporters, and polarised efflux pumps. They are used for CNS drug permeability screening and for neurovascular unit models - with the caveat that their endothelial identity is contested.
route: Primitive streak / mesoderm (or co-differentiating neural environment)
cell_types.maturation_note: Barrier phenotype appears within 8-10 days. TEER peaks about 2 days after replating onto a collagen IV/fibronectin or Matrigel-coated insert and then plateaus for about a week; astrocyte, pericyte or neuron co-culture adds a further increment within 24-48 h and keeps it elevated for up to 8 days.

morphology.endpoint: A confluent, contact-inhibited cobblestone sheet of polygonal cells with crisp, continuous junctions. Gaps, overlapping cells or ragged junctions predict low TEER whatever the staining says.

stages.label: Pluripotent monolayer
stages.look: Singularised hPSCs at a precisely controlled 35,000 cells/cm2 (defined protocol) expanded three days.

stages.label: Primitive streak
stages.look: A uniform dense monolayer after 24 h of CHIR99021; nearly every cell is brachyury+.

stages.label: Endothelial progenitors
stages.look: Still a dense sheet; VEGFR2 is nearly universal and the morphology has not yet diverged.

stages.label: Emerging endothelial islands
stages.look: Patches of clearly endothelial, polygonal cells with bright junctions, surrounded in the undefined protocol by neural progenitors and neurons.

stages.label: Purified barrier monolayer
stages.look: After replating, a uniform cobblestone sheet with continuous junctions; this is the stage for TEER and permeability assays.

markers.name: PECAM1
markers.note: Nearly 100% at day 10 in the defined protocol; expressed before VE-cadherin, as in other stem-cell-derived endothelium.

markers.name: CDH5
markers.note: Appears later than PECAM1 and is strongly induced by retinoic acid - a useful maturation readout.

markers.name: VWF
markers.note: Absent during early induction and acquired on subculture; part of the evidence the cells are vascular.

markers.name: SLC2A1
markers.note: Elevated (not merely present) GLUT-1 is the discriminator from peripheral endothelium, and it tracks with nuclear beta-catenin. Used with PECAM1 to define the BMEC population by flow.

markers.name: CLDN5
markers.note: The most informative tight-junction marker: in the defined protocol only about 60% of cells express it without retinoic acid, and non-optimal seeding density gives patchy or discontinuous junctions even when the percentage looks acceptable.

markers.name: OCLN
markers.note: Expressed by nearly all cells regardless of retinoic acid, so on its own it will not warn you about a leaky monolayer - judge distribution, not percentage.

markers.name: TJP1
markers.note: Same caveat as occludin; look for continuous junctional staining.

markers.name: ABCB1
markers.note: Nearly 100% of cells; activity and basolateral-to-apical polarisation confirmed with cyclosporin A.

markers.name: ABCG2
markers.note: Activity confirmed with Ko143; substrate accumulation rises 150-220% with inhibitor.

markers.name: ABCC1
markers.note: Activity confirmed with MK 571.

markers.name: SLC7A5
markers.note: One of the BBB-enriched transporters detected in both protocols.

markers.name: PLVAP
markers.note: Its absence is a positive sign: PLVAP is downregulated as the barrier matures and stays on in peripheral vessels.

markers.name: KRT18
markers.note: Reported as present in all cells of the differentiating population in Lippmann 2012, while K14 and p63 were absent. Central to the later claim that these cells are epithelial rather than endothelial.

markers.name: TP63
markers.note: Reported absent in Lippmann 2012; worth checking given the identity debate.

functional_assays: Transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER) on Transwell inserts
Permeability of radiolabelled sucrose, inulin, glucose, diazepam, colchicine, vincristine and prazosin
Efflux accumulation and polarised transport assays with cyclosporin A, Ko143 and MK 571
Acetylated LDL uptake
VEGF-dependent tube formation on Matrigel
TNF-alpha-inducible ICAM-1
Freeze-fracture electron microscopy of tight junction strands
Co-culture with astrocytes, pericytes and neurons for barrier induction
qc: TEER: >= 500-1,500 ohm.cm2 with astrocyte co-culture (undefined protocol) or >= 2,000-3,000 ohm.cm2 in monoculture (defined protocol); subtract an empty coated filter
Continuous junctional claudin-5, occludin and ZO-1 with no gaps
Elevated GLUT-1 in essentially all PECAM1+ cells
Functional efflux: measurable increase in substrate accumulation with each specific inhibitor, and basolateral-to-apical polarisation of P-gp
Sucrose permeability in the 10^-5 cm/min range
Seeding density held at the optimum (35,000 cells/cm2 in the defined protocol)

protocols.name: Neural/endothelial co-differentiation then selective purification
protocols.principle: hPSCs are allowed to co-differentiate in an unconditioned medium so that endothelial progenitors arise inside an embryonic-brain-like environment of neural progenitors and neurons; those neural cells supply WNT7A/WNT7B, nuclear beta-catenin accumulates in the endothelium, and the cells acquire barrier properties. A collagen IV/fibronectin matrix then selects them out.

source.authors: Lippmann ES, Azarin SM, Kay JE, et al.
source.title: Derivation of blood-brain barrier endothelial cells from human pluripotent stem cells.

protocols.efficiency: About 30% GLUT-1+/PECAM-1+ cells at 6 days of UM, rising to 66% after 2 days of EC medium (11.6 BMECs per input hPSC); essentially 100% purity after selective passaging. TEER averaged 860 +/- 260 ohm.cm2 over 30 experiments with a maximum of 1,450 +/- 140 ohm.cm2 on astrocyte co-culture; sucrose permeability 3.4 x 10^-5 cm/min
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs passaged onto Matrigel and expanded 2-3 days in mTeSR1. Cell-line-dependent yield; IMR90-4 and DF19-9-11T iPSCs purified well, H9 hESC-derived cells did not.

stages.name: Co-differentiation in unconditioned medium
stages.base_medium: Unconditioned medium (UM): DMEM/F12, 20% knockout serum replacement, 1x MEM-NEAA, 1 mM L-glutamine, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol - no bFGF
actions: Switch mTeSR1 to UM (bFGF withdrawn) to start co-differentiation
Expect major morphological change by day 5-7
stages.checkpoint: Day 6: roughly 86% of the culture is neural (23% nestin+/TUJ1-negative progenitors, 58% nestin+/TUJ1+ immature neurons, 5% neurons) with PECAM-1+ endothelial islands co-expressing GLUT-1, occludin, claudin-5 and P-glycoprotein; nuclear beta-catenin in ~40% of PECAM-1+ cells by day 5

stages.name: Selective endothelial expansion
stages.base_medium: EC medium: human endothelial serum-free medium
stages.feeding: Per schedule for 1-2 days (up to 6 days for some lines)
actions: Switch to EC medium for 2 days; this both expands the BMECs and raises GLUT-1 expression
stages.checkpoint: 66% GLUT-1+/PECAM-1+; nearly all PECAM-1+ cells now have nuclear beta-catenin and express VE-cadherin

stages.name: Matrix-based purification and monolayer formation
stages.base_medium: EC medium (20 ng/mL bFGF, 1% platelet-poor plasma-derived serum)
actions: Dissociate with dispase (2 mg/mL) and replate onto collagen IV/fibronectin-coated plates or Transwell inserts (coat plates >=30 min, inserts >=4 h at 37 C)
One well of a 6-well plate of differentiated cells seeds three wells of a 12-well plate or four Transwell inserts
stages.checkpoint: Confluent, contact-inhibited monolayer, ~100% positive for PECAM-1 and the BBB markers, with continuous ZO-1/occludin/claudin-5; acetylated LDL uptake and VEGF-dependent tube formation

stages.name: Astrocyte co-culture (barrier induction)
stages.base_medium: EC medium, or 70:30 DMEM/F12 with 2% B27 and 10% FBS
stages.feeding: Per schedule; TEER peaks at 24-48 h and stays elevated up to 8 days
actions: Co-culture the Transwell monolayer with primary rat astrocytes (HEK293 cells are the non-neural control)
Measure TEER every 24 h and subtract the value of an empty coated filter
stages.checkpoint: TEER roughly doubles with astrocytes (412 +/- 38 vs 222 +/- 51 ohm.cm2 at 24 h in EC medium; 696 +/- 8 ohm.cm2 in 10% FBS medium; up to 1,450 +/- 140 after seeding optimisation). Freeze-fracture shows tight junction strands mostly on the protoplasmic fracture face

tips: The functional panel that distinguishes these cells is the combination, not any one marker: tight junctions plus elevated GLUT-1 plus polarised efflux. P-glycoprotein, BCRP and MRP activity were all confirmed with cyclosporin A, Ko143 and MK 571.
PLVAP and SLCO1A2 transcripts were absent, which is what you want: PLVAP is downregulated as the barrier matures, and SLCO1A2/Oatp14 is rodent-specific.
Permeability of seven radiolabelled compounds correlated with in vivo rodent brain uptake at R2 = 0.98, with a 40-fold dynamic range between diazepam and sucrose.
Subculturing too early (after only 4 days of UM) gives cells that express BBB markers but never reach confluence and have malformed, discontinuous junctions.
pitfalls: Line-dependent: H9-derived BMECs could not be separated from non-brain PECAM-1+/GLUT-1-negative endothelium on collagen/fibronectin, because all endothelium likes that matrix.
The medium is undefined (knockout serum replacement, platelet-poor plasma serum), so batch and line variability in yield is expected - see Qian 2017 for the defined replacement.
Wnt inhibition with XAV-939 lowered GLUT-1+ cells from 64% to 46% but left claudin-5 and occludin untouched, so beta-catenin is only part of the specification.

Identity caveat: Lu TM, Houghton S, Magdeldin T, et al., PNAS 2021;118:e2016950118 (PMID 33542154, doi 10.1073/pnas.2016950118) report that hPSC-derived cells made this way are transcriptionally epithelial rather than endothelial and need ETS factors to acquire a true vascular fate. Treat these cultures as a barrier model, not as authenticated brain endothelium, and state which you mean.
unverified: Lippmann and colleagues tested K14, p63 and K18 epithelial markers and reported K14 and p63 absent but K18 present in all cells of the differentiating population; this is relevant to the later epithelial-identity debate and is reported here as the source states it.

protocols.name: Defined route: CHIR99021 to mesoderm, then retinoic acid
protocols.principle: Brain endothelium comes from mesoderm, so canonical WNT activation with CHIR99021 is used first to take hPSCs through primitive streak and intermediate mesoderm to endothelial progenitors; retinoic acid then confers the BBB phenotype. Everything is chemically defined and the barrier is tighter than the co-differentiation route.

source.authors: Qian T, Maguire SE, Canfield SG, et al.
source.title: Directed differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells to blood-brain barrier endothelial cells.

protocols.efficiency: Nearly 100% brachyury+ at 24 h, >90% PAX2+ at day 4, nearly 100% VEGFR2+ at day 5 and nearly 100% CD31+ at day 10; TEER above 3,000 ohm.cm2 in monoculture (around 4,000 with retinoic acid), rising a further ~30% with pericyte then astrocyte/neuron co-culture. Transcriptome correlates with primary human BMECs at r = 0.77 and expresses 206 of 234 BBB-relevant tight-junction/transporter genes
protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs singularised with Accutase and plated on Matrigel (or vitronectin/Synthemax) at 35,000 cells/cm2 in mTeSR1 with 10 uM Y-27632, then expanded three days. Seeding density is critical and 35,000 cells/cm2 was optimal for all three lines tested.

stages.name: Primitive streak induction
stages.base_medium: DeSR1: DMEM/Ham's F12, 1x MEM-NEAA, 0.5x GlutaMAX, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: canonical WNT activation; drives primitive streak

actions: Add 6 uM CHIR99021 in DeSR1 for 24 h
stages.checkpoint: Nearly 100% brachyury+ at 24 h; T and MIXL1 peak at day 2

stages.name: Mesoderm to endothelial progenitors
actions: Replace with DeSR2 and change daily to day 6
stages.checkpoint: >90% PAX2+ intermediate mesoderm at day 4; nearly 100% VEGFR2+ endothelial progenitors at day 5

stages.name: Retinoic acid-driven BBB specification
stages.base_medium: hECSR1: human endothelial serum-free medium with 1x B27

factors.name: Retinoic acid
factors.role: confers BBB phenotype; raises tight-junction and efflux transporter genes 3-20 fold

actions: Switch to hECSR1 on day 6 for two days
stages.checkpoint: CDH5 strongly induced; CLDN5, OCLN, TJP1 and ABCB1 up. Without retinoic acid only about 60% of the cells express claudin-5 and junctional distribution is patchy

stages.name: Replating and barrier formation
stages.base_medium: hECSR1 at replating, then hECSR2 (hECSR1 without retinoic acid or bFGF) from day 9

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: improves attachment, used in the no-retinoic-acid comparison

actions: Dissociate with Accutase on day 8 and replate at 1 x 10^6 cells/cm2 onto Matrigel-coated plates or Transwell inserts (collagen IV 400 ug/mL + fibronectin 100 ug/mL if differentiating on vitronectin/Synthemax)
Switch to hECSR2 on day 9 for longer-term maintenance
stages.checkpoint: TEER peaks 2 days after replating and plateaus above 2,000 ohm.cm2 through day 7; essentially 100% CD31+, with vWF, acetylated LDL uptake, VEGF-dependent tube formation and TNF-alpha-inducible ICAM-1; P-gp, BCRP and MRP accumulation assays show 150-220% increases with their specific inhibitors, and P-gp efflux is polarised basolateral-to-apical

stages.name: Neurovascular unit co-culture (optional)
actions: Co-culture day-8 cells on Transwells with primary human pericytes for 24 h, then with hPSC EZ sphere-derived astrocytes and neurons (1:3) for three more days
stages.checkpoint: A further ~30% TEER rise at day 2 and a sustained elevation versus monoculture

materials: Primary human pericytes, hPSC-derived astrocytes and neurons (optional)
tips: Seeding density is the single most sensitive parameter: only 35,000 cells/cm2 gave substantial barrier function. Other densities still gave >90% CD31+ and ~100% P-gp+ cells but with patchy claudin-5 and occludin and TEER stuck around 1,000 ohm.cm2.
Retinoic acid is not needed to make endothelium, only to make it barrier-like; it is the step to check if TEER is low but CD31 is high.
Fully defined matrices work: vitronectin performed closer to Matrigel than Synthemax did.
Compared head to head, this defined route gave higher TEER and lower batch-to-batch variation than the undefined co-differentiation protocol.
pitfalls: The mechanism by which density acts was not determined, so it has to be re-optimised empirically for a new line or lab.
Occludin and ZO-1 are expressed by nearly all cells even without retinoic acid, so those two markers will not warn you about a leaky monolayer - claudin-5 localisation and TEER will.

Identity caveat, as for Lippmann 2012: Lu TM, Houghton S, Magdeldin T, et al., PNAS 2021;118:e2016950118 (PMID 33542154, doi 10.1073/pnas.2016950118) argue these cells are misidentified epithelium that requires ETS factors for a vascular fate. The barrier phenotype is real and useful; the endothelial identity is contested.

cell_types.notes: Be explicit about what these cells are. Both protocols produce a monolayer with a barrier far tighter than primary human BMECs (339 +/- 107 ohm.cm2 in the best biopsy-derived cultures) or immortalised lines (hCMEC/D3, about 199 ohm.cm2), with correct transporter expression and polarised efflux - an excellent permeability screening platform. But Lu TM, Houghton S, Magdeldin T, et al., PNAS 2021;118:e2016950118 (PMID 33542154, doi 10.1073/pnas.2016950118) argue that cells made this way are transcriptionally epithelial rather than endothelial, and that ETS transcription factors are needed to give them a true vascular fate; the Lippmann paper itself reports cytokeratin 18 in all cells of the differentiating population. The practical consequence: call them BMEC-like or a BBB barrier model, check epithelial markers if identity matters to your claim, and do not use them as a model of brain angiogenesis. On the technical side, the defined protocol is more reproducible but extremely sensitive to one number - the initial seeding density of 35,000 cells/cm2.
